abs.strategy_reason: ABS is an SDMX 2.1 NSO; matrix confirms startPeriod is supported, so pull only periods newer than each flow's stored max(obs_date) and merge per dataflow instead of the current skip-if-file-exists full pull.
abs.vintage_signal: Per-dataflow: query GET https://data.api.abs.gov.au/rest/data/ABS,<FLOW>/all with ?startPeriod=<last_obs+1> (date-tail). For change-gating across the catalog, SDMX 2.1 supports ?updatedAfter=<last_success> on the data endpoint and df['version'] is already fetched in the sidecar (currently stored-but-never-compared) and can gate whole-flow refresh.
abs.since_param: startPeriod=<last_obs_year/period+1> on /rest/data/ABS,<FLOW>; optional updatedAfter=<last_success_iso> to scope changed flows
abs.out_paths_note: Multi-file: one parquet per dataflow at data/clean_full/abs/<FLOW>.parquet (~1222 files) plus sidecar data/clean_full/abs_catalog.parquet. Requires replacing the line ~434 existence-skip with read-existing-then-merge.
abs.rate_note: No API key. API is flaky (drops mid-body) - keep 5x exponential backoff on IncompleteRead/429/5xx; hardcoded UA; no rate-limit param.
abs.open_question: Is df['version'] (already captured in the sidecar) reliable enough to gate whole-flow refresh, or must we rely on startPeriod date-tail per flow? Confirm whether ABS honors updatedAfter on the data endpoint.

adb.strategy_reason: ADB KIDB is SDMX 3.0 and the matrix confirms startPeriod is accepted on the data URL; annual cadence makes deltas cheap, so fetch only periods after each flow's max(obs_date) and merge per dataflow.
adb.vintage_signal: Date-tail per flow: append &startPeriod=<last_obs_year+1> to GET /v4/sdmx/data/{agency},{flow}/{freq}.{code}.?format=sdmx-csv. No clean vintage/version feed is exposed, so re-pull at startPeriod=last_year for changed-flow safety; _dataflows.json catalog cache detects newly added flows.
adb.out_paths_note: Multi-file: one parquet per dataflow at data/clean_full/adb/<FLOW>.parquet (~59) plus sidecars _dataflows.json, _economies.json, _empty/<FLOW>.txt. Empty flags can permanently suppress flows that later gain data - clear _empty on delta runs.
adb.rate_note: No API key. Full-flow dumps 504 (must go per-indicator); 422/504 -> per-economy fallback; 1.0s RATE sleep between calls; 429 -> 60s sleep. Self-throttling makes runs slow.
adb.open_question: Given annual cadence + tiny size, is per-flow SDMX delta worth the merge refactor, or is overwrite_if_changed (re-pull whole flow yearly) operationally simpler? No reliable per-flow vintage signal exists to gate overwrite, which is why I chose delta.

barro_lee.strategy_reason: Static academic dataset of 15 hardcoded GitHub Pages CSVs rebuilt into one parquet; a 'delta' is meaningless - re-fetch and overwrite the single parquet only when the upstream files move.
barro_lee.vintage_signal: HTTP conditional on each barrolee.github.io CSV (ETag / Last-Modified via If-Modified-Since), or the GitHub commit SHA of the barrolee.github.io Pages repo. Currently the script exits immediately if barro_lee.parquet exists (line ~159) and never re-fetches - add the conditional check.
barro_lee.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/barro_lee/barro_lee.parquet (~239K obs). In-run dedup already handles overlapping MF/F/M aggregate files.
barro_lee.rate_note: No API key, no rate limits (0.3s courtesy sleep). Only blocker is upstream URL/file-name changes (15 paths hardcoded).
barro_lee.open_question: When Barro-Lee publish a new vintage they may change file names / version prefix (BL_v3_* -> v4); the hardcoded 15-path list won't auto-discover that. Acceptable to require a human to bump the file list on a new release?

bcb.strategy_reason: BCB SGS API natively accepts dataInicial/dataFinal (already used for the daily-406 fallback), so compute max(obs_date) per series and fetch only newer rows - far better than the current skip-sid resume that never extends existing series.
bcb.vintage_signal: Date-tail / always-fetch recent: per series read existing bcb.parquet max(obs_date), request dataInicial=max_date+1..today. No upstream vintage feed; freshness is the date tail itself.
bcb.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/bcb/bcb.parquet (~300 curated series). MUST add (series_key,obs_date) dedup before append - current code appends with no dedup, so wiring deltas onto an existing series will duplicate unless dedup is added (today only the skip-sid path avoids dupes).
bcb.rate_note: No API key. Daily series reject full-history (HTTP 406) -> chunk into 9-year windows; 429 -> 60s sleep; 0.3s RATE between series.
bcb.open_question: Curated ~300-series list is hardcoded (not the full SGS catalog) - should new SGS series be auto-discovered, or is the curated list intentional and frozen?

bcrp.strategy_reason: BCRP API URL is /{code}/json/{start}/{end} and fetch_series() already takes start/end, so compute max(obs_date) per series and fetch start=max_date+1 - the current skip-if-key-present logic never extends a daily series (stale for a daily source).
bcrp.vintage_signal: Date-tail always-fetch: per series read existing bcrp.parquet max(obs_date), set start=max_date+1, end=today. No vintage feed; the daily date tail is the signal.
bcrp.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/bcrp/bcrp.parquet (6 daily FX series). Needs (series_key,obs_date) dedup on append - current append has none and relies on the series-key skip to avoid dupes.
bcrp.rate_note: No API key. Only daily PD* series work (monthly/quarterly PN* return empty); single-series requests only (batching fails); 0.5s RATE; 3 retries linear backoff; Spanish month-name date parsing.

bea.strategy_reason: BEA GetData currently hardcodes Year=ALL but the API accepts specific Year values, so a date filter (Year=prior..current) IS feasible; read each group parquet's max(obs_date) and re-pull only recent years, merging into the group file.
bea.vintage_signal: Date-tail by Year: per group read max(obs_date) and call with Year=<that_year>..<current> instead of ALL. No BEA-wide vintage/last-modified feed; recent-year re-pull-and-merge is the freshness mechanism. (Note: each _ingest_* helper hardcodes Year='ALL' + full pq.write_table overwrite, so this is a non-trivial refactor.)
bea.since_param: Year=<max_obs_year..current_year> on GetData (per dataset: NIPA/Regional/etc.); MNE already loops Year so plug max_year there
bea.out_paths_note: Multi-dir/multi-file: one parquet per table/cube under data/clean_full/bea/<dataset>/<group>.parquet (~600 files across 12 dataset dirs - NIPA 252, Regional 105, etc.). State in data/raw/bea/_done_groups.json; manifest data/raw/bea/catalog_manifest.json must pre-exist (this script does not build it).
bea.rate_note: REQUIRES BEA_API_KEY (SystemExit if missing). BEA caps 100 req/min, 100MB/min, 30 err/min; in-code limiter holds <=85 req/min and <=70MB/min across 6 workers; 429/5xx backoff; error code 8 (volume quota) retried hard.
bea.open_question: Errors are swallowed as empty [] and can silently write a 0-row group that is then marked done and skipped under --resume (data-loss-by-silence). Should the delta refactor fail loudly on empty responses rather than marking the group done?

bfs.strategy_reason: BFS is PxWeb and the query already enumerates each table's time dimension via filter:item, so only the last N periods can be requested per table - matches the PxWeb/startPeriod delta pattern rather than the current full ~673-table rebuild.
bfs.vintage_signal: PxWeb time-value selection: request only the most-recent time codes per table (filter:item on the 'time' dimension) and merge. PxWeb table metadata (GET /api/v1/de/<dbid>) exposes the latest available time values / an 'updated' timestamp that can gate per-table refresh. No combined-file vintage exists today (script holds all series in memory and overwrites one bfs.parquet).
bfs.since_param: filter:item on the time dimension restricted to values > last stored period (PxWeb has no startPeriod; you select recent time codes explicitly)
bfs.out_paths_note: Currently single file: data/clean_full/bfs/bfs.parquet (~14MB, ~673 tables, German /de data endpoint). Delta requires restructuring to per-table parquets (or read-back + per-series max date) since there is no resume and the every-50-tables in-place checkpoint truncates the file on crash.
bfs.rate_note: No API key. English /en endpoint only lists; data must use German /de (English returns 400 for table data). MAX_CELLS=100000 guard down-samples oversized tables to aggregates by design; 0.3s RATE; 429 -> 30s sleep.
bfs.open_question: Does the BFS PxWeb metadata expose a reliable per-table 'last updated' timestamp to gate refresh, or must we always request the recent time tail for all ~673 tables? Also confirm the MAX_CELLS down-sampling is acceptable to keep under delta.

bis.strategy_reason: Two scripts: the primary CBS/LBS path (ingest_bis_cbs_lbs.py) downloads whole-table flat-CSV zips with NO date filter, so gate on HEAD Last-Modified/Content-Length and re-download+rebuild only when the zip changes; the secondary SDMX path (ingest_bis_full.py) could do sdmx_delta via startPeriod but degrades to per-flow re-pull and both scripts write to the same dir - bulk_snapshot is the binding strategy for the source.
bis.vintage_signal: HTTP HEAD Last-Modified / Content-Length on the two bulk zip URLs (data.bis.org CBS.zip & LBS.zip) - the zips ARE dated upstream but the code reads no date today. Replace the >10000-byte download skip and the out_path-exists ingest no-op with a HEAD-gated re-download. (SDMX path ingest_bis_full.py: optional startPeriod=<last_year> on /data/{flow}, but BIS exposes no clean per-flow vintage so it degrades to full re-pull.)
bis.since_param: n/a for bulk CBS/LBS (no date param); SDMX path would use startPeriod=<last_obs_year> on /data/{flow}
bis.out_paths_note: Multi-file AND multi-script collision: ingest_bis_cbs_lbs.py writes data/clean_full/bis/CBS.parquet (37.5MB) & LBS.parquet (183MB) with raw zips cached in data/raw/bis_bulk; ingest_bis_full.py writes WS_*.parquet (giants chunked as <DID>__<FREQ>[__<VAL>].parquet) into the SAME data/clean_full/bis dir plus _manifest.json/_catalog.json. Force-refresh must clear BOTH the cached zips (>10000B skip) and the parquets (out-exists no-op); deleting only the parquet rebuilds from the STALE cached zip.
bis.rate_note: No API key. Polite custom UA. License bis-attrib-nc (non-commercial, attribution). Bulk: 600s timeout, resumable HTTP Range (LBS zip ~356MB). SDMX: per-socket 120s timeout, 5x retry, CHUNK_WORKERS=6 (BIS throttles per-connection bandwidth on big extracts).
bis.open_question: Two scripts share data/clean_full/bis - should CBS/LBS migrate to the SDMX ingest_bis_full.py path (enabling startPeriod deltas and removing the bulk-zip dependency), or keep the bulk-zip snapshot path as the source of record? Confirm CBS.zip/LBS.zip URLs return a usable Last-Modified header.

bls.strategy_reason: BLS ships whole-history flat files (<survey>.data.*) with no per-row update date and no server-side date filter (true since= needs the API connector); gate on per-file IIS directory sizes and re-download+rebuild only changed surveys.
bls.vintage_signal: BLS IIS directory file sizes captured by jobs/_bls_build_manifest.py into data/raw/bls/_manifest.json (the download() size-match skip); a changed upstream file size triggers re-download. Note: the parse/build step is gated by a per-survey resume sidecar, so a refresh must also clear/-force the <survey>.meta.json sidecars to actually rebuild changed surveys.
bls.out_paths_note: grouped: one parquet per survey under data/clean_full/bls/<survey>.parquet (~67 surveys, biggest cb 286MB) plus <survey>.meta.json resume sidecar; raw cache data/raw/bls/<survey>/. Two scripts exist: ingest_bls.py is authoritative (cross-file dedup, date32, manifest-gated); ingest_bls_full.py is legacy (no dedup -> QCEW double-count, obs_date as string) and writes to the SAME dir -- do NOT run it for refreshes.
bls.rate_note: No API key; custom User-Agent REQUIRED (BLS blocks generic UAs). 300s download timeout, 5x backoff. Prerequisite: data/raw/bls/_manifest.json must exist (run _bls_build_manifest.py first) or main() crashes on json.load.
bls.open_question: To pick up new periods on already-built surveys, the orchestrator must run _bls_build_manifest.py to refresh sizes AND pass --force (or clear *.meta.json sidecars); confirm that is acceptable cost weekly given the large refresh (~1GB+ across surveys) vs. a Current-only top-up that would need new code.

boe.strategy_reason: The IADB CSV endpoint accepts a server-side Datefrom filter, so we can request only obs since last stored date and append+dedup per prefix; the hardcoded DATETO is a vintage date to compute as today, not a real blocker.
boe.vintage_signal: date-tail always-fetch: per <prefix>.parquet read max obs_date, request Datefrom=(last_obs - small overlap); upstream has no separate change feed, so the date-tail request itself is the freshness probe. Series universe additions still require re-running jobs/_boe_enumerate.py.
boe.since_param: Datefrom (IADB CSV query param; DATEFROM/DATETO as DD/Mon/YYYY, e.g. Datefrom=01/Jan/2026); currently hardcoded full-range 01/Jan/1963 -> 01/Jun/2026 and the hardcoded DATETO must become computed today.
boe.out_paths_note: grouped by 3-char series-code prefix: <prefix>.parquet under data/clean_full/boe/ (~37 families, 116 files = parquet+.done+.titles.json each). Input universe data/raw/boe/_series_codes.json from jobs/_boe_enumerate.py. Today process_prefix rewrites the whole prefix parquet via .part+os.replace; wiring last-obs lookup + append/dedup by (series_key,obs_date) is a moderate change.
boe.rate_note: No API key; custom UA. ~50 series per CSV request (batch=50); 300s timeout, 5x retry; endpoint returns an HTML error page (not CSV) on bad/empty requests (body must start with 'SERIES'). ThreadPoolExecutor capped at 6 workers (polite).
boe.open_question: Per-prefix .done resume files currently SKIP completed prefixes; for date-extend mode they must be ignored in favor of a max-obs-date check. Also confirm acceptable overlap window for the Datefrom dedup, and how often to re-run _boe_enumerate.py to catch newly added series codes.

bundesbank.strategy_reason: Bundesbank XML API IGNORES startPeriod/endPeriod (no usable date delta), so every pull is whole-flow; only 7 medium flows, so re-fetch full XML and overwrite the flow parquet atomically only when a vintage signal moved.
bundesbank.vintage_signal: HEAD/conditional GET on each flow's SDMX data URL -- check Last-Modified / ETag on the per-flow response, or compare parsed max obs_date to stored; no published manifest exists, so a per-flow Last-Modified header is the cheapest change probe before committing the ~full download.
bundesbank.out_paths_note: one parquet per flow under data/clean_full/bundesbank/<flow>.parquet for 7 hardcoded flows (BBEX3, BBNZ1, BBDP1, BBSIS, BBFI1, BBFI3, BBBP1). Whole flow built in a Python list then pq.write_table (non-atomic -- no .tmp+replace; add atomic write). BBEX3 response ~1.3GB XML buffered fully in memory (OOM risk).
bundesbank.rate_note: No API key (keyless DL-DE-BY-2.0); custom UA + Accept: application/xml. RATE=2.0s sleep between flows; 600s timeout, 3x retry.
bundesbank.open_question: Does the Bundesbank per-flow endpoint actually return a reliable Last-Modified/ETag for change detection? If not, this degrades to unconditional whole-flow re-pull monthly. Also: the <1000-row auto-stub-delete re-pulls legitimately tiny flows (BBFI3 ~4.7KB) every run -- confirm intended.

cboe.strategy_reason: CBOE CDN serves only full-history *_History.csv (no date filter) but the whole dataset is tiny (~888KB, refresh in seconds); for a daily-cadence source the right move is to always re-fetch and overwrite the single parquet, gated on the CSV vintage signal.
cboe.vintage_signal: HEAD Last-Modified / ETag on each index's *_History.csv on the CBOE CDN (e.g. VIX_History.csv); since cost is trivial, can also just unconditionally overwrite cboe.parquet each run (the current skip-if-exists must be removed -- it makes the daily source never update).
cboe.out_paths_note: single combined parquet -> data/clean_full/cboe/cboe.parquet for ~20 volatility indices (series_key e.g. VIX, VIX_CLOSE). All rows in memory then one pq.write_table; in-run dedup via seen set on (key,obs_date). pq.write_table is non-atomic (no .tmp+replace -- add atomic write).
cboe.rate_note: No API key (free for informational use, CBOE terms); custom UA. 60s per-CSV timeout, 0.3s politeness sleep. NO retry/backoff -- a transient CDN failure silently drops that index from the build.
cboe.open_question: Must remove the skip-if-exists early-exit (or it never updates). Add retry on the per-index GET so a transient CDN failure does not silently drop an index from the daily build. Does the CDN return usable Last-Modified, or should we just overwrite unconditionally each day?

cbs_nl.strategy_reason: CBS OData catalog exposes a per-table 'Modified' field already retrieved by get_catalog (used only as Title today); gate each table re-pull on Modified vs a stored manifest and overwrite the per-table parquet only when it moved.
cbs_nl.vintage_signal: The 'Modified' timestamp per table from opendata.cbs.nl/ODataCatalog/Tables -- compare to a stored manifest of last-seen Modified per tableId; today the code reads Modified but never uses it for freshness (per-table gate is only os.path.exists).
cbs_nl.out_paths_note: per-table files -- one {tableId}.parquet per CBS table under data/clean_full/cbs_nl/ (~2180 files); huge tables flush {tableId}.part{i}.parquet + {tableId}.ckpt.json then concatenate. WARNING: dir currently has 139 leftover .ckpt.json + 164 .part*.parquet -- a plain re-run RESUMES mid-download tables from saved $skip rather than starting clean.
cbs_nl.rate_note: No API key (keyless OData). Sleeps 60s on 503/429, 0.5s between pages, 0.3s between tables; UA identifies the library.
cbs_nl.open_question: Wiring needed: replace the os.path.exists short-circuit with a Modified-vs-manifest comparison, and clean up the 139 stale .ckpt.json/164 .part files (resume relies on STABLE $skip order -- if upstream reorders between runs the resumed offset can double-count/drop). Note OData v3 supports $filter on Period, so a future S2 date-extend is possible but not wired.

census.strategy_reason: Census API natively supports time=from+YYYY and the script already enumerates YEAR/year slices, so we can fetch only years >= stored max obs_date and append; the fetch side is ready, only start-year selection and append-vs-overwrite need wiring.
census.vintage_signal: date-tail: per dataset read existing parquet max obs_date (or _manifest.json) and request time=from+<maxYear>; also clear cached data/raw/census/data.json + ts_meta.json to detect NEW datasets (catalog is cached and otherwise hides new tables). No upstream change feed -- the dated re-request is the probe.
census.since_param: time=from+YYYY (and the YEAR/year+quarter enumeration start) -- e.g. time=from+2025; today hardcoded time=from+1900 (entire history).
census.out_paths_note: per-dataset files -- one parquet per timeseries dataset, safe_name(path) ('timeseries/' stripped, '/'->'__', e.g. qwi__sa.parquet) under data/clean_full/census/ (~83 files) plus _manifest.json (append-only run log, duplicate path entries). Default (no --resume) OVERWRITES each parquet via a fresh pq.ParquetWriter at outpath; true append needs code change.
census.rate_note: REQUIRES CENSUS_API_KEY from D:/research/econfindatalibrary/.env (SystemExit if missing; present). get= capped ~50 vars (chunked 45), ~400k cells/query (QWI); HARD_DEADLINE=120s/request; per-dataset budget 1800s default (2400s intltrade base). Metadata probe 6 workers.
census.open_question: Many datasets currently write truncated=true (budget-capped partial coverage); a date-extend that trusts max obs_date will inherit those gaps -- backfill/raise --budget first. Also confirm appending (vs the current truncate-on-write) is acceptable, and that multi-chunk position-based variable merge is stable enough to append safely.

central_banks.strategy_reason: Two of three providers expose server-side date filters (BoC Valet ?start_date=, Riksbank /Observations From/To); fetch only obs since stored max date and append. SNB cube CSV has no date param but is cheap -- overwrite per cube within the same job.
central_banks.vintage_signal: date-tail per provider: BoC/Riksbank request start_date/From = stored max obs_date (the dated request is the probe); SNB has no since-param so re-download each cube CSV and overwrite (gate optionally on the cube CSV Last-Modified). The os.path.exists skip must be replaced with a max-date check.
central_banks.since_param: BoC Valet /observations ?start_date=YYYY-MM-DD ; Riksbank /Observations From=YYYY-MM-DD (To optional); SNB = n/a (whole-cube CSV only).
central_banks.out_paths_note: MULTI-DIR, NOT under a central_banks/ dir: data/clean_full/boc/boc.parquet (single), data/clean_full/riksbank/riksbank.parquet (single), data/clean_full/snb/{cube_id}.parquet (one per cube, ~24 hardcoded SNB_CUBES). Writers are write-once; must switch to read-existing+append+dedup (no dedup logic exists today -- naive append would duplicate).
central_banks.rate_note: All keyless. BoC 0.3s/batch (20 series/batch); SNB RATE_SNB=1.0s/cube; Riksbank deliberately ~0.5 req/s, 2s sleeps, aggressive 429 backoff (10*(attempt+1)s). SNB cube IDs hardcoded -- new cubes need editing SNB_CUBES.
central_banks.open_question: Append path + dedup by (series_key,obs_date) must be added per provider (none today). Confirm SNB stays full-overwrite per cube (no date param). Riksbank picks the first non-empty of d/m/q/y frequencies -- ensure the date-extend uses the same stored frequency per series to avoid mixing.

cepii_baci.strategy_reason: BACI is a whole-vintage zip of annual CSVs with no delta API; a new release restates all prior years, so re-download+rebuild the full vintage, gated on detecting a new V-string vintage on the CEPII download page.
cepii_baci.vintage_signal: Scrape/poll the CEPII BACI download page for the latest vintage V-string in the zip filename (currently hardcoded BACI_HS17_V202401b.zip / BACI_HS96_V202401b.zip); a new V-string = new data. Per-vintage gate is os.path.exists of the parquet + >1MB cached-zip size check. No change feed; polling the download page is the only signal.
cepii_baci.out_paths_note: single-file-per-vintage: baci_hs17.parquet and baci_hs96.parquet under data/clean_full/cepii_baci/; raw zips data/raw/cepii_baci/{HS17,HS96}.zip. Streamed in 500k-row batches via one ParquetWriter per vintage; .part download renamed atomically.
cepii_baci.rate_note: No key; direct download verified 200 OK. Large download (timeout=600s, streamed); single GET per vintage, no rate limit.
cepii_baci.open_question: Vintage discovery is not automated -- the FILES dict is hardcoded to V202401b and nothing detects new releases (effectively manual today). Worth confirming a human will bump FILES, or building the CEPII-page scraper. CRITICAL: if FILES is updated but the cached raw zip is NOT cleared, the >1MB size check passes and the OLD vintage is silently reused.

cepii_gravity.strategy_reason: Whole-file dated bulk download (Gravity_csv_V202211, hard-coded) with no date filter; a hard-coded versioned URL is S5/S1 not S6, and a new release is a new whole zip — gate on the file and re-download+rebuild only when the vintage changes.
cepii_gravity.vintage_signal: HEAD on the active GRAVITY_URLS file (CEPII http(s)://www.cepii.fr/.../Gravity_csv_V202211.zip) for Last-Modified/Content-Length; or scrape the CEPII Gravity download page for the latest V-string version token and compare to the stored one.
cepii_gravity.out_paths_note: single file: data/clean_full/cepii_gravity/cepii_gravity.parquet (download buffered in memory, 500MB cap, no raw cache).
cepii_gravity.rate_note: no key; 500MB in-memory download cap (aborts if exceeded); tries http/https + Gravity-then-GeoDist fallback (degraded run can silently write the thinner GeoDist subset).
cepii_gravity.open_question: Confirm the canonical CEPII Gravity listing URL to poll for new V-vintages, and decide whether to alert when the run falls back to the smaller GeoDist file instead of full Gravity.

cftc.strategy_reason: Weekly COT and the matrix's own incremental_path: switch to the CFTC Socrata publicreporting API which accepts a server-side $where report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd > last date filter for a true since=last_obs delta, then append/merge.
cftc.vintage_signal: Date-tail always-fetch: query Socrata with $where report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd > stored max obs_date; new weekly rows appear when present. (Legacy bulk path would instead need HEAD on per-year deahistfo{year}.zip / fut_disagg_txt_{year}.zip for the current year.)
cftc.since_param: $where=report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd > '<last_obs_date>' on the CFTC Socrata/publicreporting endpoint (current code uses per-year zips with no date param).
cftc.out_paths_note: single wide union-schema file: data/clean_full/cftc/cot_all.parquet (all cols as strings); raw zips cached under data/raw/cftc/. Watch de-dup on report-week key — historical combined + per-year zips can overlap and duplicate rows.
cftc.rate_note: no key (US public domain); Socrata app token optional but recommended to lift throttle; current zip path 404s unpublished years gracefully.
cftc.key_env: none (optional SODA_APP_TOKEN if migrating to Socrata)
cftc.open_question: Migrate to the Socrata API (true date delta, needs a per-week de-dup key) versus keep per-year zips with always-refetch of the current year? Confirm the exact Socrata dataset id(s) covering both legacy and disaggregated reports.

cnb.strategy_reason: Daily FX served as per-year files via ?year=YYYY; steady state fetches only the current year (the date tail), and the in-function (key,date) seen-set already de-dups for a clean merge into the stored max obs_date.
cnb.vintage_signal: Date-tail always-fetch: re-pull current year's fixing file (BASE?year=<current_year>) every run and merge rows with obs_date > stored max; the current-year file always contains the newest daily rates.
cnb.since_param: ?year=YYYY path param (fetch year >= year(max obs_date), i.e. just the current year in steady state); CNB exposes no finer date filter.
cnb.out_paths_note: single file: data/clean_full/cnb/cnb.parquet; series_key = CNB_FX:{CCY}_CZK, rates normalized per-1-unit. No append path today (full rebuild) — add read-existing + append.
cnb.rate_note: no key; keyless HTTPS; 0.2s sleep between years; UA header set; per-year HTTP errors logged and skipped.
cnb.open_question: On Jan 1 boundary, fetch both prior and current year for one run to avoid missing late-December rows — confirm that handling is acceptable. Also confirm the 'amount' multiplier header regex won't silently drop a currency if CNB changes header format.

comtrade.strategy_reason: Annual trade totals; UN Comtrade fetch_totals supports a server-side &period=YYYY[,YYYY] filter, so a real since=last_obs delta is computing missing years per reporter and appending (matrix's incremental_path).
comtrade.vintage_signal: Server-side period filter: for each reporter request &period=<years from max(obs_date)+1 .. current> and append only returned new annual periods (Dec-31). No separate manifest.
comtrade.since_param: &period=YYYY[,YYYY,...] on comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview (current resume key is series_key/reporter only, which wrongly skips existing reporters — must change skip key to (reporter, period)).
comtrade.out_paths_note: single file: data/clean_full/comtrade/comtrade.parquet (~24k rows, 713 series, annual Dec-31). CRITICAL FIX: resume keyed on series presence silently never extends existing reporters to new years.
comtrade.rate_note: no key (public preview endpoint); ~100 req/hr free tier; script self-throttles RATE=2.0s, BATCH=20, 429 backoff 60s*attempt.
comtrade.key_env: none (optional COMTRADE_KEY for the authenticated higher-rate endpoint)
comtrade.open_question: Change the resume/skip key from reporter to (reporter, period) and add &period — confirm. Should we move to the authenticated Comtrade API key for higher rate limits given the per-reporter year backfill?

cow.strategy_reason: Static academic releases delivered as whole-history versioned bulk ZIP/CSVs with hard-coded filenames (NMCv7.zip, COW_Trade_4.0.zip, States2024.zip) and no date param; a new release is a new whole file — gate per-file and rebuild only the changed dataset.
cow.vintage_signal: HEAD on each correlatesofwar.org/wp-content/uploads/<file>.zip for Last-Modified/Content-Length, and/or scrape the COW dataset pages for a new version token (e.g. NMCv8, COW_Trade_5.0). Note SSL verify is disabled (expired cert) — HEAD must use the same relaxed TLS.
cow.out_paths_note: MULTIPLE files: one parquet per dataset under data/clean_full/cow/ — nmc.parquet, trade.parquet, wrp.parquet, alliances.parquet, mids.parquet, states.parquet, igo.parquet + _cow_log.txt. Each gated independently.
cow.rate_note: no key; SSL verify=False (expired/mis-issued COW cert; urllib3 warnings disabled); RATE=0.5s; hard-coded versioned filenames 404 silently on rename.
cow.open_question: Per-dataset version bumps require editing filenames; want an automated probe of likely next versions (NMCv8, COW_Trade_5.0) plus alert-on-404? Also alliances/states have hard-coded end-year caps (2016/2025) that may truncate recent years on a new release.

cso.strategy_reason: CSO PxStat ReadDataset returns whole tables with NO startPeriod param (so not SDMX-delta-able), but the Navigation.Search catalog carries per-table release-date metadata — gate on that release date and overwrite only changed tables/subjects.
cso.vintage_signal: Refresh _catalog.json each run via PxStat Navigation.Search and compare each table's release/last-modified field (e.g. RlsLiveDatetimeFrom / RlsArchiveFlag) against the stored value; re-pull and overwrite only tables whose release date moved.
cso.since_param: n/a (ReadDataset has no startPeriod; whole-table re-pull on change, no server-side date filter)
cso.out_paths_note: MULTIPLE files: ~46 per-subject-group parquets keyed by SbjCode (e.g. 26_Labour_Market.parquet, 29_National_Accounts.parquet) + cached _catalog.json. A changed table maps into its owning subject parquet — must read-existing + append + dedup on (key,date) rather than skip whole subject.
cso.rate_note: no key (ws.cso.ie JSON-RPC + REST); self-throttle RATE=0.4s; 429 handled with 30s sleep; stale cached _catalog.json silently freezes the table universe — must refresh it each run.
cso.open_question: Confirm the exact PxStat catalog field that reliably signals a table revision (RlsLiveDatetimeFrom vs RlsArchiveFlag vs a modified timestamp), and move from per-subject-file skip to per-table changed-detection so existing subjects gain new periods.

damodaran.strategy_reason: Annual cross-sectional snapshots re-estimated each January (not an appendable time series); a small single file that a re-run rebuilds correctly — drop the existing-file early-return and overwrite atomically when a new vintage is detected.
damodaran.vintage_signal: Probe the date-stamped country-premium filename for the new month/year (ctryprem<Mon><YY>.xlsx, currently ctrypremApr26.xlsx) and HEAD Last-Modified on the stable-name sheets (betas.xls, wacc.xls, ...) at pages.stern.nyu.edu; new January release = new ctryprem file present.
damodaran.rate_note: no key (pages.stern.nyu.edu); needs openpyxl + xlrd; fetch bails on 403/404 and requires >500 bytes; 0.5s between files.
damodaran.open_question: Auto-discover the rotating ctryprem<Mon><YY> filename (probe Jan/Apr current-year variants) so a new annual vintage is picked up without a human edit — confirm the naming pattern Damodaran uses each year.

defillama.strategy_reason: Daily, but every phase re-fetches the full history (which always includes the newest day) and overwrites its parquet idempotently — a plain re-run already refreshes catalog/overview/chains/tvl correctly; gate is implicit-newest-day, no date param exists.
defillama.vintage_signal: Poll-only: re-pull the full series from api.llama.fi / yields.llama.fi each run (totalDataChartBreakdown, historicalChainTvl, protocol/pool charts) and overwrite — newest day is implicit in the full history. No ETag/manifest/since filter is offered upstream.
defillama.since_param: n/a (no since/startPeriod; full-history endpoints, overwrite per run)
defillama.out_paths_note: MULTIPLE files (~113): catalog parquets, per-(type,dataType) overview files, chains_tvl.parquet, stablecoins_total/circulating.parquet, tvl_protocol_shard00-29 (30) and yields_pool_shard00-59 (60) built from _yields_stage.jsonl. Stray legacy bridge_aggregators_snapshot.parquet on disk.
defillama.rate_note: no key; MAXW=6; yields endpoint heavily throttled (~0.5 req/s), single worker default (DL_YIELDS_WORKERS to raise); 429/5xx retry+backoff with Retry-After.
defillama.open_question: Yields is the trap: _yields_stage.jsonl resumes by pool not by date, so already-staged pools never get new days; and hash(slug)%N sharding depends on PYTHONHASHSEED, risking cross-run shard drift/duplication. Need a fix (per-(pid,date) append + stable hash/PYTHONHASHSEED=0 + single process) before yields can be trusted as a daily delta.

dst.strategy_reason: DST /v1/data has NO startPeriod param (always send full time selection), so per-table re-pull whole history and overwrite the per-subject parquet only when the catalog's 'updated' timestamp moved.
dst.vintage_signal: GET https://api.statbank.dk/v1/tables?lang=en -> per-table 'updated' field; capture last-run timestamp and refresh only tables (hence their subject parquet) whose updated > last_run.
dst.since_param: n/a (DST /v1/data has no startPeriod; full time selection POSTed every call)
dst.out_paths_note: Writes ~705 per-subject-group parquets under data/clean_full/dst/ (one per table-id prefix, e.g. AKU110.parquet). Granularity blocker: skip is per-subject-file, so refreshing one table forces rebuilding that whole subject parquet (read existing + append + (key,date) dedup, then atomic overwrite).
dst.rate_note: No API key (api.statbank.dk). Self-throttle RATE=0.3s; 429 -> 30s sleep. MAX_CELLS=50,000 cap silently collapses large multi-dim tables to TOT/first values.
dst.open_question: Per-subject-file skip currently means re-runs add nothing; wiring the per-table 'updated' gate requires changing skip from per-subject to per-table-changed. Also confirm the 50k-cell cap lossiness is acceptable (won't expand on refresh).

ecb.strategy_reason: ECB is SDMX 2.1 (data-api.ecb.europa.eu) and the URL builders already accept &startPeriod/&endPeriod; do updatedAfter detection + startPeriod=last_obs+1 delta merged per dataflow.
ecb.vintage_signal: Per dataflow/chunk: ?updatedAfter=<last_success_iso> to detect changed flows; then pull deltas. Catalog re-fetched each run to _catalog.json. (Operational daily path already runs a separate connectors/ecb delta, not the bulk jobs/ingest_ecb.py.)
ecb.out_paths_note: ~542 grouped parquets under data/clean_full/ecb/: <AGENCY>__<FLOW>[__<FREQ>[__<VAL>[__<YEAR>]]].parquet plus _manifest.json/_catalog.json. Giants (EXR/MIR/YC/QSA/CSEC) shard into freq/sub/decade parts; deltas land as new dated parts per chunk and must dedup on (series_key,obs_date). NOT one dir per unit.
ecb.rate_note: No API key. Global gate MIN_INTERVAL=0.6s (env ECB_MIN_INTERVAL); 429 -> 20s cooldown. Workers 1-6 (default 4). Timeouts FULL=1800s/CHUNK=900s/MEGA=1500s; SERIES_CAP=3,000,000 per file; staging at data/raw/ecb/_tmp.
ecb.key_env: ECB_MIN_INTERVAL (optional throttle override); no auth key
ecb.open_question: Whole-flow path (url_all) lacks a startPeriod variant and BatchWriter overwrites on finalize; delta needs read-existing+merge (or dated delta parts). Confirm whether to wire delta into jobs/ingest_ecb.py or keep delegating to connectors/ecb (the actual daily runner).

edgar_13f.strategy_reason: New quarter = new dataset key on the SEC data-sets page; per-period partitioning (period=<key>) makes new quarters pure additions, so set --from=<last_key+1q> and only fetch keys newer than on disk.
edgar_13f.vintage_signal: Scrape SEC data-sets PAGE_URL (regex '<key>_form13f.zip') to enumerate published keys; a new key appearing = new quarter. NOTE: re-publication of an existing quarter is NOT detected (no Last-Modified check on existing keys).
edgar_13f.since_param: --from <last_processed_key + 1 quarter> (client-side date-key tail; SEC page itself exposes no date param). Compute max key from existing period= dirs via key_sort_value; do NOT trust _manifest.json (datasets_processed is empty/stale).
edgar_13f.out_paths_note: Multi-dir: data/clean_full/edgar_13f/<TABLE>/period=<datasetKey>/<TABLE>.parquet for 7 tables (SUBMISSION, COVERPAGE, OTHERMANAGER, OTHERMANAGER2, INFOTABLE, SIGNATURE, SUMMARYPAGE). INFOTABLE is the ~118M-row holdings table. Raw zip cache at data/raw/sec_edgar/form13f/.
edgar_13f.rate_note: No API key but SEC REQUIRES descriptive User-Agent ('Econ-Fin Data Library admin@hfdatalibrary.com'); fair-access limits -> 0.3s sleep, 4-attempt backoff. License gate assert_reservable('us-public-domain') must pass.
edgar_13f.key_env: none (User-Agent string required, not an env key)
edgar_13f.open_question: Should re-published (revised) existing quarters be detected/refreshed (would need a per-key Last-Modified/size check)? Default --from is 2020q1, so full history needs an early --from.

edgar_jrc.strategy_reason: EDGAR publishes whole-history country-total workbooks (1970..latest) per annual release; no date param. Re-fetch the known files, gate on a vintage signal, and atomically overwrite the single parquet only when the vintage moved.
edgar_jrc.vintage_signal: HEAD Last-Modified/Content-Length on the hard-coded GHG_BASE/AP_BASE file URLs (e.g. IEA_EDGAR_CO2_1970_2024.zip, v81_FT2022_AP). Detects re-publication of the current vintage; a brand-new annual filename (e.g. 2026 release) is NOT auto-detectable and needs a human URL bump (this is hardcoded-URL, NOT a hard block -> not S6).
edgar_jrc.since_param: n/a (whole-history annual vintage, no since param)
edgar_jrc.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/edgar_jrc/edgar_jrc.parquet (series_key EDGAR:{gas}:{iso3}, annual Dec-31). No raw cache, no per-gas files. Side logs _edgar_jrc_log.txt/_err.txt.
edgar_jrc.rate_note: No API key. JRC JEODPP FTP (jeodpp.jrc.ec.europa.eu) can 403/404 (treated fatal-skip per file) and is slow (300s timeout, 3 retries, 5s*attempt backoff).
edgar_jrc.open_question: How to auto-detect a NEW annual release whose filename embeds a new year range (currently human-edited GHG_BASE/AP_BASE)? Also fix latent bug: ingest_dataset returns int 0 on failure vs 4-tuple on success, so failed gases are silently dropped; and main() early-exits when parquet exists (must delete to pick up a new vintage).

ei_statreview.strategy_reason: Energy Institute publishes the full 1965..latest panel each annual edition (no since param); re-fetch and atomically overwrite the single parquet when a new edition is detected.
ei_statreview.vintage_signal: HEAD Last-Modified/Content-Length on the primary EI all-data XLSX URL (energyinst.org __data/assets/excel_doc/<id> path). Caveat: the asset id is version-specific and rotates per edition, so a dead primary silently falls through the hard-coded fallback list to the OWID mirror (different schema/units).
ei_statreview.since_param: n/a (whole-history annual panel, no since param)
ei_statreview.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/ei_statreview/ei_statreview.parquet (series_key EISR:{variable}:{country}, annual Dec-31). No raw cache, no per-variable files. Side logs _ei_statreview_log.txt/_err.txt.
ei_statreview.rate_note: No API key. 180s timeout; one attempt per URL then next fallback (no retry/backoff within a URL).
ei_statreview.open_question: The EI asset URL changes yearly (embedded asset id) and must be refreshed by a human; need a way to discover the new edition's URL and to ALERT on silent fallback to the OWID mirror (which shifts variable naming/coverage without failing).

eia.strategy_reason: EIA bulk zips are whole-series snapshots with NO date param; the public manifest gives a per-dataset last_updated, so re-download+rebuild only datasets whose last_updated advanced past the stored value.
eia.vintage_signal: GET https://api.eia.gov/bulk/manifest.txt -> per-dataset 'last_updated' + 'accessURL'. Compare vs stored data/clean_full/eia/_summary.json last_updated; skip dataset when manifest last_updated <= stored.
eia.since_param: n/a (per-dataset whole-zip snapshot; obs-level since not possible without re-downloading the full zip)
eia.out_paths_note: Grouped, two dirs: one data parquet per dataset at data/clean_full/eia/<DATASET>.parquet AND one meta sidecar at data/clean_full/eia/_meta/<DATASET>.parquet, plus _summary.json. Raw zips cached at data/raw/eia/<DATASET>.zip. ~316M obs; EBA/AEO.<year> are the giants (EBA streams, never whole in RAM).
eia.rate_note: No API key (bulk manifest + accessURL public). 600s per-download timeout, 5-try quadratic backoff. Without --skip-download every run RE-DOWNLOADS all zips (bandwidth waste) since download()'s size-skip is never triggered in main().
eia.open_question: Wire the manifest last_updated gate (read _summary.json, skip unchanged datasets) to avoid daily full re-download; --skip-download currently reuses zips regardless of freshness (stale risk), and a parse error leaves the prior dataset parquet stale (not refreshed).

ember.strategy_reason: Each Ember CSV is a whole long-format table republished in full with no date param; the GCS object listing exposes per-object updated/size, so re-download+rebuild only CSVs whose updated/size changed.
ember.vintage_signal: GET https://storage.googleapis.com/storage/v1/b/emb-prod-bkt-publicdata/o?prefix=public-downloads/ -> per-object 'updated' + 'size'; diff each against the saved data/raw/ember/ember_manifest_full.json and only fetch changed objects.
ember.since_param: n/a (whole CSV re-published; no since param)
ember.out_paths_note: Grouped, one parquet per source CSV: data/clean_full/ember/<dataset_id>.parquet (~59 files) plus _summary.json. Catalog cached at data/raw/ember/ember_manifest_full.json. ~8.1M obs.
ember.rate_note: No API key (GCS bucket openly listable/downloadable). ThreadPoolExecutor max_workers=6, 5-try exponential backoff; listing paged 1000/req. No rate-limit blockers observed.
ember.open_question: write_parquet only writes when n_obs>0, so a CSV that empties/disappears upstream leaves a stale prior parquet; decide whether the freshness gate should also prune removed objects. Generic-melter fallback can change series_key composition if upstream columns change.

epu.strategy_reason: Each policyuncertainty.com workbook is republished as a full Year/Month history (no since param) and all ~22 feed a single combined parquet; re-pull all workbooks monthly and atomically overwrite (in-run (series_key,date) dedup already exists).
epu.vintage_signal: HEAD Last-Modified/Content-Length per workbook on the ~22 hard-coded policyuncertainty.com /media/*.xlsx URLs (poll to decide whether to re-pull); since output is a single combined file, simplest robust approach is to re-pull all workbooks on the monthly cadence and overwrite.
epu.since_param: n/a (full Year/Month workbook re-published; no since param)
epu.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/epu/epu.parquet (series_key EPU:{clean_colname}:{code}; All_Country uses EPU:epu:{country}, 1st-of-month). No raw cache, no per-country files. Side logs _epu_log.txt/_err.txt.
epu.rate_note: No API key. fetch = 3 attempts, 3s*attempt backoff, 60s timeout; 403/404 fatal-skip per URL. policyuncertainty.com asset URLs occasionally change/redirect -> a dead URL silently drops that country.
epu.open_question: CRITICAL: main() early-exits when epu.parquet exists, so the monthly cadence adds NO new months without deleting the file or adding a --force/overwrite path. License is 'free for academic use' only (NOT a reservable/commercial class) — flag before publishing commercially.

eurostat.strategy_reason: One of the 4 named giants; the TOC catalogue carries a per-dataset lastUpdate change-feed, so refresh only whole dataset codes whose lastUpdate moved instead of the blind skip-if-exists crawl.
eurostat.vintage_signal: Eurostat TOC catalogue (catalogue/toc/txt) per-dataset lastUpdate/lastModified column; persist code->lastUpdate state map and re-fetch only codes whose upstream lastUpdate is newer (plus brand-new codes).
eurostat.since_param: n/a (no obs-level since; unit-level change-feed via TOC lastUpdate, not startPeriod — this profile is the bulk SDMX-TSV dissemination path, format=TSV&compressed=true, not the per-obs SDMX query API)
eurostat.out_paths_note: WRITES TO TWO DIRS/STAGES: raw data/raw/eurostat/<code>.tsv.gz (~7,640 files, fetch_eurostat_bulk.py) AND clean_full/eurostat/<CODE>.parquet (~7,753 files, separate ingest_eurostat.py). A true delta must purge/refetch only changed raw codes then reparse only those in ingest (today ingest reparses ALL; its advertised --delta flag is a no-op).
eurostat.rate_note: No key. Polite UA, 6 concurrent workers, 4 retries linear backoff on 429/5xx, 300s timeout, atomic .part->replace. Constraint is sheer volume (~7,600 datasets, multi-GB, ~6.1B obs); legacy files/ bulk path is 410 Gone.
eurostat.open_question: Confirm the TOC txt lastUpdate field is reliably populated per code so the change-feed can drive unit-level refresh; and decide whether ingest_eurostat.py should be patched to honor a changed-codes list (its --delta currently does nothing).

famafrench.strategy_reason: 8 full-history Ken French factor zips with no since param; per-dataset parquet overwrite is idempotent and factors are re-published whole each month, so gate on a zip vintage signal and overwrite only when upstream moved.
famafrench.vintage_signal: HTTP Last-Modified / If-Modified-Since (or ETag) on each Dartmouth factor zip URL; conditional GET and rebuild the per-dataset parquet only on 200 (not 304). Today there is NO vintage check and a double exists-guard (cached zip + parquet) makes a plain re-run a no-op.
famafrench.out_paths_note: 8 grouped parquet at data/clean_full/famafrench/<name>.parquet (factors_3/5 monthly+daily, momentum monthly+daily, st/lt reversal monthly); raw zips cached at data/raw/famafrench/. To refresh, BOTH the cached zip and the parquet exists-guards must be removed/conditional-gated (deleting only one is insufficient).
famafrench.rate_note: No key. UA set; single GET per file with NO retry/backoff, 60s timeout, non-200 -> dataset silently skipped (logs success even when several skipped as 'already'). Add retry resilience.
famafrench.open_question: Does the Dartmouth host return a usable Last-Modified/ETag on the factor zips? If not, fall back to re-download + content-hash compare. License is research/educational only (not a reservable/commercial class) — note in source.

faostat.strategy_reason: Bulk full-domain zips with NO server-side date filter; FAO publishes a machine manifest (datasets_E.json) with FileRows/FileSize per domain, so gate on the manifest and re-download+rebuild only changed domains.
faostat.vintage_signal: https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/datasets_E.json — persist each domain's FileRows/FileSize (manifest entry) and skip re-download+re-parse of domains whose entry is unchanged. Script currently downloads without reading any date/size field.
faostat.out_paths_note: Per-domain grouped parquet data/clean_full/faostat/<DatasetCode>.parquet (68 files) + _ingest_summary.json sidecar; raw zips cached at data/raw/faostat/<CODE>.zip (68). clean_full is unconditionally overwritten per run; the stale-data trap is the raw-zip cache (existing zip is reused, updates silently missed) — must clear raw or gate on manifest.
faostat.rate_note: No key. CC-BY-4.0, custom UA, HTTP backoff on 429/5xx (max 5 tries, up to 60s). No documented rate limit but downloads are multi-GB zips (network/disk bound, refresh cost 'large').
faostat.open_question: Is FileRows/FileSize in datasets_E.json a reliable change indicator (vs a lastUpdated/date field if present)? Prefer a date field if the manifest exposes one to avoid same-size republications going undetected.

fdic.strategy_reason: The FDIC API supports server-side REPDTE range filters (already used as filters=REPDTE:[lo TO hi]); read max(obs_date) from financials.parquet and fetch only REPDTE:[last+1 TO today], appending.
fdic.vintage_signal: Date-tail / always-fetch the open quarter: compute max(obs_date) from existing financials.parquet and request the next REPDTE window; meta.total drives pagination. No last-modified header needed since the date filter is authoritative.
fdic.since_param: filters=REPDTE:[<last_obs+1> TO <today>] (REPDTE range filter on the financials endpoint)
fdic.out_paths_note: Per-endpoint parquet data/clean_full/fdic/{financials,institutions,history,failures,summary}.parquet. ONLY financials (LONG, series_key=CERT={cert}:{field}) is date-extendable via REPDTE+append (_append_parquet exists); institutions/summary/history/failures are WIDE snapshots that still need full overwrite. No raw dir.
fdic.rate_note: No key (public domain). PAGE=10000, 0.3s sleep between pages, 4 retries with 5*(attempt+1)s backoff, no documented hard limit. NOT in daily_update SCHEDULE/BULK_SCRIPTS — currently manual-run only, no orchestrated cadence.
fdic.open_question: Replace the 'if output exists: return' early-return guards with max-date + filtered append (today a re-run never extends and a killed mid-financials run can leave a partial file the next run treats as done). Confirm desired cadence and wire into the scheduler (currently unorchestrated).

fed_board.strategy_reason: Each release is served as a whole ZIP via Output.aspx?rel=<REL>&filetype=zip with no date filter; store an HTTP ETag/Last-Modified per release and re-download+reparse only changed releases.
fed_board.vintage_signal: Per-release HTTP ETag / Last-Modified on datadownload/Output.aspx?rel=<REL>&filetype=zip (skip download+parse when unchanged); plus re-scrape the DDP home (discover_releases) to catch newly-added releases. Today there is no etag/last-modified check — the full release is always re-downloaded.
fed_board.out_paths_note: Per-release grouped parquet data/clean_full/fed_board/<REL>.parquet + <REL>__series.parquet + <REL>.meta.json + _summary.json (18 releases); raw zips at data/raw/fed_board/<REL>.zip. CRITICAL: default (no --force) run is a no-op for any release with an existing .meta.json, so a scheduled run skips done releases and never picks up new obs without --force.
fed_board.rate_note: No key (US public domain). Custom UA on requests.Session, 5 tries backoff min(60,3*(attempt+1)^2), validates the zip contains *_data.xml. No rate limit; downloads are large (Z.1 alone ~590MB).
fed_board.open_question: daily_update wires fed_board as 'daily' via run_connector --since, but the standalone ingest_fed_board.py does NOT parse --since (uses the generic connector path). Confirm which path actually runs in prod, and ensure the scheduled invocation forces refresh (or honors an etag gate) rather than no-op'ing on existing .meta.json.

fhfa.strategy_reason: 9 full-history snapshot files (CSV/XLSX) at fixed fhfa.gov URLs with no date param; build fully overwrites every cube, so gate each file on Last-Modified/hash and rebuild only changed cubes.
fhfa.vintage_signal: HTTP Last-Modified / ETag (or content hash) on each of the 9 fixed fhfa.gov file URLs (e.g. /hpi/download/monthly/hpi_master.csv); re-download + rebuild only files whose signal changed. Today --download overwrites raw unconditionally with no freshness check.
fhfa.out_paths_note: MULTIPLE CUBES: data/clean_full/fhfa/<cube>.parquet for 9 cubes (hpi_master, hpi_at_3zip_quarterly, annual_national/state/cbsa/county/zip3/zip5/tract) + per-cube __series.parquet + <cube>.meta.json + top-level fhfa.meta.json; raw at data/raw/fhfa/ (9 files). build() overwrites every cube (idempotent).
fhfa.rate_note: No key (US public domain). urllib3 Retry(total=5, backoff 1.5 on 429/5xx) + inner 3-attempt loop, 0.5s polite sleep. No rate limit. Scheduled refresh MUST pass --download (default/no-flag run only builds from possibly-stale raw); a failed download leaves the OLD raw file and build silently uses stale raw for that one file.
fhfa.open_question: Some FHFA quarterly cubes (e.g. hpi_at_3zip_quarterly) update quarterly while HPI master is monthly — confirm a single monthly cadence is acceptable or split per-cube. Also confirm static-URL files reliably expose Last-Modified for the gate.

frankfurter.strategy_reason: The Frankfurter API accepts arbitrary start..end date ranges (start_date already used per-year); read max(obs_date) and fetch only max_date+1..today instead of re-pulling 1999..now every run.
frankfurter.vintage_signal: Date-tail always-fetch: read max(obs_date) from frankfurter_fx_eur.parquet and request /{max_date+1}..{today}; in-memory dedup by (series_key, day) already makes the merge safe. No header needed.
frankfurter.since_param: /{<max_obs_date+1>}..{<today>} (Frankfurter start..end range path; start_date param already in use)
frankfurter.out_paths_note: Single grouped parquet data/clean_full/frankfurter/frankfurter_fx_eur.parquet (series_key e.g. EURUSD, obs_date, value). No raw dir, no sidecar. Single-file overwrite (or concat+rewrite for the incremental change).
frankfurter.rate_note: No key. Free api.frankfurter.app (ECB rates, license ecb-attrib-nomodify). Custom UA, 0.25s sleep between requests, 5 retries exp backoff cap 30s. No documented rate limit; polite single-threaded.
frankfurter.open_question: daily_update schedules it 'daily' via run_connector --since but the standalone script ignores --since (re-pulls full history). Confirm which path runs; the cheap fix is the single since..today loop change. None blocking.

fraser_efw.strategy_reason: Genuinely un-auto-fetchable RIGHT NOW: all 5 hardcoded edition URLs are dead (2024/2023 xlsx 404, efwdata.com DNS NameResolutionError, GitHub mirror 404); no working source exists and no parquet has ever been written. Needs a human to supply a current EFW download URL.
fraser_efw.vintage_signal: none-poll-only: no working endpoint to poll. Detection of a new EFW edition currently requires a human to find/supply a live Fraser Institute or efwdata.com download URL; once a working URL exists this could become overwrite_if_changed (new annual vintage URL / Last-Modified).
fraser_efw.out_paths_note: Intended single grouped parquet data/clean_full/fraser_efw/fraser_efw.parquet (series_key EFW:{component}:{iso}, obs_date Dec-31 of year, value). CURRENTLY no parquet exists — only _fraser_log.txt / _fraser_err.txt. In-memory (series_key,date) dedup when working.
fraser_efw.rate_note: No key. CC-BY-4.0. Blocker is the SOURCE (dead URLs + DNS failure), not auth/rate. Not in daily_update SCHEDULE/BULK_SCRIPTS — manual run only, no cadence.
fraser_efw.open_question: HUMAN ACTION REQUIRED: supply the current working Fraser Institute / efwdata.com EFW dataset xlsx download URL. The script silently logs 'All URLs failed' and exits ~0 with no error artifact beyond the log, so an orchestrator sees no failure — also add a non-zero exit / alert when all URLs fail.

fred.strategy_reason: fredgraph.csv accepts server-side cosd/coed date params, so fetch only obs after each series' stored max date and append; matrix flags this as 'feasible and important' since current skip-if-exists leaves all ~290 series stale forever.
fred.vintage_signal: date-tail always-fetch: no ETag/Last-Modified on fredgraph.csv; per series compute max(obs_date) from fred.parquet and request rows after it. Re-fetch ALL series each run (not just missing) gated by the per-series max-date filter.
fred.since_param: cosd={max_obs_date+1} (start date) on https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id={series_id}; coed optional as end bound
fred.out_paths_note: Writes ONLY data/clean_full/fred/fred.parquet (single grouped parquet: series_key, obs_date, value). SHARES the fred/ dir with the separate fred_releases source which owns release_*.parquet + _manifest.json — do NOT touch those when refreshing fred, and vice-versa.
fred.rate_note: Keyless endpoint, rate-sensitive: RATE=0.5s sleep/series, 3 retries (30s wait on 429). Custom UA+Accept required. No documented hard cap but throttle to avoid 429.
fred.open_question: SERIES is a hardcoded ~290-id curated list (some duplicate/typo ids 404 harmlessly) — confirm whether the curated list should stay fixed or be expanded; new series outside the list are never discovered.

fred_releases.strategy_reason: v2 release/observations endpoint supports observation_start, so per release fetch only obs after stored max date and merge; /releases is re-enumerated each run to also catch brand-new release_ids.
fred_releases.vintage_signal: date-tail always-fetch per release (seed observation_start from each release's stored max obs_date); plus GET fred/v2/releases each run to detect new release_ids not yet in _manifest.json. No per-release Last-Modified is exposed.
fred_releases.since_param: observation_start={max_obs_date+1} threaded into params at fred/v2/release/observations (currently only release_id+next_cursor are sent)
fred_releases.out_paths_note: Writes ONLY per-release files data/clean_full/fred/release_NNNNN.parquet (~180 files) + _manifest.json in the SAME fred/ dir as the separate fred source. fred.parquet belongs to ingest_fred.py — must NOT be deleted here. Manifest currently marks 0-obs releases 'done', hiding releases that may later be populated.
fred_releases.rate_note: FRED_API_KEY required (Bearer for v2). Self-throttles sleep 0.1s/page, 0.3s/release, 0.2s/release-list page; 300s per-page timeout. No geo block.
fred_releases.open_question: _manifest.json marks releases with 0 public-domain obs as 'done' (n==0 branch) so they are never re-attempted — should the delta refresh periodically re-probe these in case upstream adds public-domain series later?

freedomhouse.strategy_reason: Single small (~12KB) annual wide XLSX (1973-present) with no date-filtered endpoint; correct refresh is to re-pull the newest edition and overwrite, gated on a vintage signal. Not S6 — the URL is merely hardcoded, the file is freely re-fetchable.
freedomhouse.vintage_signal: HEAD Last-Modified / Content-Length on the current year-stamped XLSX (e.g. freedomhouse.org/.../2025-03/Country_and_Territory_Ratings_and_Statuses_FIW_1973-2025.xlsx); to catch a NEW edition, probe the freedomhouse.org FIW download page for the latest year-stamped path each ~Feb/Mar.
freedomhouse.out_paths_note: Single file data/clean_full/freedomhouse/freedomhouse.parquet (series_key=political_rights:/civil_liberties:/freedom_status:Country). Write is non-atomic (no .tmp) — add atomic replace.
freedomhouse.rate_note: Keyless direct XLSX from freedomhouse.org, UA header, 120s timeout. Risk: hardcoded CDN path 404s when FH reorganizes — no fallback discovery. openpyxl required.
freedomhouse.open_question: New annual edition uses a NEW year-stamped XLSX URL that is not auto-discovered — need an agreed way to detect/derive the next edition's URL (or a human adds it each Feb/Mar).

fsi_fundforpeace.strategy_reason: Single small (~33KB) annual index; the multi-year GitHub tidy CSV mirror is the resilient de-facto full source and exposes a clean commit-level vintage signal, so re-pull+overwrite when the mirror moves. No date endpoint; not S6 (freely fetchable).
fsi_fundforpeace.vintage_signal: GitHub commit SHA / API Last-Modified for raw.githubusercontent.com/ksreyes/tidy-fragile-states-index CSV (GET /repos/ksreyes/tidy-fragile-states-index/commits?path=<csv> HEAD SHA); fall back to HEAD on the per-year fragilestatesindex.org XLSX if the mirror is unreachable.
fsi_fundforpeace.rate_note: Keyless; GitHub raw + fragilestatesindex.org. 30s timeout, 0.5s sleep/year. fragilestatesindex.org WordPress upload paths are version-specific/fragile; GitHub mirror is the resilient fallback.
fsi_fundforpeace.open_question: Reliance on a community GitHub mirror (ksreyes) — if that repo goes stale or disappears, freshness depends on fragile per-year fragilestatesindex.org XLSX URLs; confirm the mirror is acceptable as primary.

gapminder.strategy_reason: Output is a single grouped 14MB parquet rebuilt wholesale from a community GitHub repo with no date filter; gate on the repo HEAD commit SHA and re-crawl+overwrite atomically only when the SHA moves. (File-level compare-API delta is a valid optimization but the base strategy is overwrite-on-change.)
gapminder.vintage_signal: GitHub commits API HEAD SHA for open-numbers/ddf--gapminder--systema_globalis (GET /repos/open-numbers/ddf--gapminder--systema_globalis/commits/HEAD); compare to stored SHA, no-op if unchanged. Optional: /compare/{old}...{new} to re-parse only changed datapoint CSVs.
gapminder.out_paths_note: Single file data/clean_full/gapminder/gapminder.parquet (series_key={indicator}:{geo}). Built fully in memory then one non-atomic pq.write_table — no checkpoint/resume; a late crawl failure loses all progress. FLUSH_EVERY constant is defined but unused.
gapminder.rate_note: Unauthenticated GitHub = 60 req/min HARD limit (handles 403 by 60s sleep+retry); hundreds of CSVs + RATE=0.2s/file make a cold pull slow. Adding GITHUB_TOKEN would raise to 5000/hr but code does not read one. get_file_list uses recursive=0 which can truncate very large trees.
gapminder.key_env: none (GITHUB_TOKEN recommended to lift the 60/min cap)
gapminder.open_question: Should we add GITHUB_TOKEN and switch get_file_list to recursive=1 to avoid tree truncation/rate stalls on full re-crawls? Not in daily_update SCHEDULE — confirm intended cadence/trigger.

gcb.strategy_reason: Global Carbon Budget is re-estimated yearly with whole-series back-revisions, so append-merge is unsafe — correct semantics is full overwrite per vintage. No date filter; gate on the Zenodo latest-version record. Not S6: files are freely fetchable once URLs are bumped.
gcb.vintage_signal: Zenodo concept-DOI 'latest version' record id (the GCB Zenodo record, currently 14106218 -> a new id each vintage) via the Zenodo API; plus the globalcarbonbudget.org download page for the current /download/NNNN/ ids. Re-download+overwrite all four parquets when the latest Zenodo version changes.
gcb.out_paths_note: MULTI-FILE under data/clean_full/gcb/: gcb_budget.parquet, gcb_national_fossil.parquet, gcb_luc.parquet, gcb_fossil_flat.parquet. Each guarded by its own os.path.exists; if URLs are bumped without deleting all four, a partial run can leave a MIX of vintages — must overwrite all four together. Non-atomic writes.
gcb.rate_note: Keyless; globalcarbonbudget.org redirecting /download/NNNN/ links + zenodo.org. 120s timeout, 3 retries w/ backoff, 1s sleep between components.
gcb.open_question: globalcarbonbudget.org download-ids and Zenodo record-ids change EVERY vintage — confirm we drive refresh off the Zenodo concept-DOI 'latest' record (stable across versions) rather than the hardcoded numeric ids, and that all four component URLs are bumped atomically.

ggdc.strategy_reason: PWT and Maddison releases are complete static panels with whole-panel revisions between versions, so refresh = whole-file overwrite per version (version prefixes keep series disjoint). No date filter; gate on the Dataverse dataset version / rug.nl file. Not S6: GET works (only HEAD 403s).
ggdc.vintage_signal: Per source: Dataverse dataset version + datafile id for PWT11 (datafile 554105) and Maddison2023 (421302) via the dataverse.nl API; HEAD Last-Modified on rug.nl/ggdc/docs/pwt100.xlsx and .../maddison/data/mpd2020.xlsx. Re-pull+overwrite a component only when its pinned datafile id / Last-Modified changes.
ggdc.out_paths_note: MULTI-FILE under data/clean_full/ggdc/: pwt10.parquet, pwt11.parquet, maddison2020.parquet, maddison2023.parquet (series_key prefixed PWT10:/PWT11:/MADDISON:/MADDISON23:). Each guarded individually; per-version overwrite is safe (disjoint prefixes). Non-atomic writes. NOTE separate source_ids penn_world_table/maddison/pwt have their own scripts and dirs — not this batch.
ggdc.rate_note: Keyless; rug.nl + dataverse.nl/api/access/datafile/{id}. 120s timeout, 3 retries, requires response >10KB, 1s sleep between versions. Dataverse HEAD returns 403 but GET works.
ggdc.open_question: A future PWT12 / Maddison2026 needs a NEW Dataverse datafile id + a new ingest_* function added by a human — no auto-discovery of new releases; confirm a human is alerted when a new PWT/Maddison vintage ships.

gii.strategy_reason: Currently un-auto-fetchable: all 5 hardcoded URLs return HTTP 404 (verified _gii_log.txt 2026-06-09), no parquet exists, and there is NO live URL to poll — a human must re-point the source to a live WIPO/mirror file before any automation can run. Once repaired the natural strategy is overwrite_if_changed (annual single XLSX, gate on a vintage signal).
gii.vintage_signal: none-poll-only at present (every candidate URL is dead, so nothing live to gate on). Post-repair: HEAD/commit-SHA on whichever live source is found (e.g. the wipo-analytics/gii-data GitHub repo path, which appears renamed/moved, or the live wipo.int XLSX for the latest edition).
gii.out_paths_note: Intended single file data/clean_full/gii/gii.parquet (series_key=GII:{indicator}:{iso3}) — CURRENTLY ABSENT; dir holds only empty _gii_log.txt/_gii_err.txt. Non-atomic write when working.
gii.rate_note: Keyless; 120s timeout, 1s sleep between candidates, openpyxl for XLSX branch. ACTIVE BLOCKER: all sources 404.
gii.open_question: REQUIRES HUMAN: find a currently-live GII source and repair the URLS list. Likely candidate is the renamed/moved wipo-analytics/gii-data GitHub repo (verify its current path/branch) or the latest wipo.int wipo_pub_2000_20XX XLSX; until then the source produces zero output.

gleif.strategy_reason: Access is a single whole 'latest' golden-copy zip with no per-record date filter; gate on the file's freshness and re-download+rebuild only when it moves.
gleif.vintage_signal: HTTP HEAD on https://leidata.gleif.org/api/v1/concatenated-files/lei2/latest/zip and compare Last-Modified / Content-Length (GLEIF refreshes ~3x/day); only re-pull when either changes vs the value stored at last successful ingest.
gleif.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/gleif/lei_records.parquet (~85MB, ~3.3M rows); raw zip cached at data/raw/gleif/gleif_golden_copy.zip — must clear BOTH on force-refresh or the zip-skip re-ingests the stale snapshot.
gleif.rate_note: No key/auth; large streamed download, timeout 600s, UA header set; no documented rate limit.
gleif.open_question: GLEIF also publishes a daily 'latestDelta' golden-copy that would allow LEI-keyed UPSERT; want full snapshot (current design) or switch to delta upsert to cut bandwidth?

gpi.strategy_reason: Tiny annual full table (series_key/obs_date/value) cheapest to overwrite wholesale; no observation-level since-param exists for an annual Excel report, so gate on a vintage signal and overwrite atomically.
gpi.vintage_signal: HEAD/ETag/Last-Modified on the (repaired) live IEP/OWID GPI source URL once it exists; until then there is no usable signal because every hardcoded GPI_URL 404s.
gpi.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/gpi/gpi.parquet (currently absent — only _gpi_log.txt/_gpi_err.txt exist).
gpi.rate_note: No key; UA header set, 2 retries per URL.
gpi.open_question: BLOCKER: all 9 hardcoded GPI_URLS return 404, so the source produces no parquet and exits success silently. Need a working IEP/OWID GPI URL before any strategy can run — please supply the current download link.

gppd.strategy_reason: Small (~700KB) static cross-section whole table that a re-run rebuilds correctly; no upstream date param, so gate on a vintage signal and overwrite the single parquet only when the release changes.
gppd.vintage_signal: GitHub commit SHA / Last-Modified on the master CSV mirror (and/or WRI dataverse dataset version metadata); GPPD is effectively frozen at WRI v1.3.0 (2021), so changes are rare.
gppd.rate_note: No key; UA header, timeout 120s; primary WRI dataverse URL may 404 over time (falls back to GitHub mirrors).
gppd.open_question: WRI has not released past v1.3.0; confirm we keep polling the GitHub mirror SHA indefinitely vs treating it as a frozen one-time snapshot.

gus_bdl.strategy_reason: BDL /data/by-variable accepts a server-side 'year' filter, so fetch only years newer than the stored last_obs per K-subject and upsert rather than the current skip-if-exists which never captures new years.
gus_bdl.vintage_signal: date-tail always-fetch: read max(year) from each existing K{n}.parquet and request only year>=that from the API (no last-modified header on BDL); merge new (series_key,obs_date) rows.
gus_bdl.out_paths_note: per-K-subject files data/clean_full/gus/K1.parquet … K54.parquet (~33 files) plus _catalog.json; matrix source_id is 'gus' (script jobs/ingest_gus_bdl.py) — distinct from gus_dbw.
gus_bdl.rate_note: No key; RATE=0.12s between calls + 429 handling (sleep 60s); full crawl is tens of thousands of calls (hours/days) — the year-filter delta is what makes ongoing refresh affordable.
gus_bdl.open_question: _catalog.json is cached indefinitely, so brand-new variables/subjects won't appear under a pure date-tail refresh — confirm an acceptable cadence to invalidate the catalog cache to pick up new variables.

gus_dbw.strategy_reason: The /variable-data-section call already filters by id-rok (year); for refresh re-sweep only the latest 1-2 years and UPSERT into the area parquet keyed on (series_key,obs_date) instead of the binary done-flag skip.
gus_dbw.vintage_signal: date-tail always-fetch: store per (var,section) the max year seen and re-fetch only id-rok > that (no last-modified exposed); fetch_year already dedups via a 'seen' set.
gus_dbw.out_paths_note: per-area files area_{id}.parquet built from parts/area_{id}/v{var}_s{sec}.parquet, plus _cache/, _checkpoint.json, logs/gus_dbw.DONE sentinel; area_15.parquet alone ~109MB — writes to multiple dirs (clean_full/gus_dbw + parts + _cache + logs).
gus_dbw.rate_note: Optional GUS_DBW_CLIENT_ID (X-ClientId) raises rate tier; anonymous is severe (5/s, 100/15min, 1000/12h, 10000/7d → SLEEP=45s; registered → 9s; 429 → sleep 900s). Anonymous full crawl takes weeks — incremental year-tail is essential.
gus_dbw.key_env: GUS_DBW_CLIENT_ID (optional, strongly recommended to drop gap 45s→9s)
gus_dbw.open_question: Checkpoint model is binary done/not-done; converting to per-section last_refreshed_year is required for delta. Is registering for a GUS_DBW_CLIENT_ID acceptable so refreshes finish in reasonable time?

hagstofa.strategy_reason: PxWeb source: tables expose an 'updated' timestamp and accept selection queries, so detect changed tables via 'updated' and re-POST only recent time-dim values, upserting per database — the PxWeb analogue of updatedAfter/startPeriod.
hagstofa.vintage_signal: PxWeb per-table metadata 'updated' field (GET table metadata at https://px.hagstofa.is/pxis/api/v1/...): compare each table's 'updated' to last ingest, re-pull only changed tables.
hagstofa.since_param: PxWeb selection 'values' filter on the time dimension (post only the latest period codes, i.e. period >= last_obs+1); no literal startPeriod query string — selection is a POSTed JSON query.
hagstofa.rate_note: No key; RATE=0.3s between calls, 429 → sleep 30s; MAX_CELLS=100000 caps large tables (silently aggregates non-time dims — coverage limit, not a refresh blocker).
hagstofa.open_question: _catalog.json cached indefinitely so new tables/databases won't appear without invalidation; and the MAX_CELLS auto-aggregation means some series are already truncated — confirm whether to raise the cell cap when adding incremental support.

harvard_atlas.strategy_reason: Full annual CSV snapshots downloaded and rewritten whole with no observation-level since-param; gate on the Dataverse dataset version and overwrite each per-dataset parquet only when a new vintage publishes.
harvard_atlas.vintage_signal: Dataverse dataset API by DOI (doi:10.7910/DVN/XTAQMC, NDDMSN, YAVJDF) — compare latest versionNumber / publicationDate (and resolve current datafile IDs automatically) vs last ingest; current code pins FIXED numeric file IDs so it silently re-uses the old vintage.
harvard_atlas.out_paths_note: 9 per-dataset files: eci_rankings.parquet, services_country_year.parquet, services_cp_{1,2,4,6}.parquet, hs12_country_year.parquet, hs12_cp_{hs1,hs2}.parquet — refresh is NOT atomic across the 9 (per-job try/except can leave some fresh, some stale).
harvard_atlas.rate_note: No key (public Dataverse access endpoint); UA header, timeout 180s, 4 retries with backoff, RATE=0.3s between jobs.
harvard_atlas.open_question: Hardcoded datafile-ID constants must be replaced with DOI-version resolution to ever pick up a new Atlas vintage; approve adding the Dataverse DOI metadata lookup so refresh isn't a manual code edit?

ibge.strategy_reason: SIDRA v3 REST takes an explicit period list (/periodos/{periods}); read max(obs_date) per aggregate, fetch only newer periods from /periodos, and concat-rewrite the parquet instead of the current unconditional skip. (REST, not SDMX, so S2 not S3.)
ibge.vintage_signal: date-tail via the aggregate's /periodos endpoint: GET https://servicodados.ibge.gov.br/api/v3/agregados/{agg}/periodos, take periods > stored max(obs_date), fetch only those (no last-modified header exposed).
ibge.since_param: period path segment on /agregados/{agg}/periodos/{period1|period2|...} (restrict the period list to new periods)
ibge.out_paths_note: per-aggregate files data/clean_full/ibge/<agg_id>.parquet (~8221 files observed); pq.write_table writes directly with no .tmp+rename, so a crash mid-write can leave a corrupt file that is then skipped forever — add atomic write when converting to delta.
ibge.rate_note: No key; self-imposed 0.5s sleep between requests, 4-retry backoff; INCLUDE_MUNI=False hard-codes out municipality level N6 (only N1+N3 fetched) — coverage limit.
ibge.open_question: Confirm we keep INCLUDE_MUNI=False (municipal N6 excluded) under the incremental design, and approve switching pq.write_table to atomic .tmp+rename to avoid the corrupt-then-skipped-forever trap.

idb.strategy_reason: CKAN datastore_search has no since filter so any update means re-pulling a whole resource; but CKAN resource metadata carries last_modified, so re-fetch only CHANGED resources gated on that signal rather than skipping all existing ones.
idb.vintage_signal: CKAN package_show -> resource['last_modified'] (and revision_id) per resource at data.iadb.org; compare against stored last_modified sidecar / parquet mtime, re-download+overwrite only resources where upstream last_modified is newer.
idb.out_paths_note: Multi-file: writes ~555 per-resource parquets to data/clean_full/idb/<pkg_slug>__<resource_id[:8]>.parquet (one dir, many files; new rid => new file).
idb.rate_note: No key (open CKAN). RATE=0.3s between requests; explicit 60s sleep on HTTP 429. Resources >500,000 rows intentionally skipped; datastore_active=False skipped. Re-run still calls package_show for ~217 packages each run.
idb.open_question: Confirm CKAN last_modified is reliably populated/advanced on row updates at data.iadb.org (some CKAN portals leave it null); if unreliable, fall back to periodic full re-pull of large/important packages.

ilostat.strategy_reason: The rplumber bulk endpoint returns the WHOLE indicator table with no since/start param, but the TOC publishes per-indicator n.records; re-pull+overwrite only indicators whose record count grew, gating on a manifest comparison.
ilostat.vintage_signal: Re-download TOC data/raw/ilostat/toc_indicator_en.csv (rplumber.ilo.org); per id compare TOC n.records against manifest 'rows'/'expected'; if TOC count exceeds recorded rows, re-pull that id's full parquet and overwrite atomically.
ilostat.out_paths_note: Multi-file: ~1947 per-indicator-frequency parquets at data/clean_full/ilostat/<id>.parquet, plus run state data/raw/ilostat/_manifest.csv and TOC data/raw/ilostat/toc_indicator_en.csv (single output dir).
ilostat.rate_note: No key (rplumber.ilo.org bulk API). Concurrency capped at 6 workers; per-request timeout 900s; 5-retry exp backoff honoring 429; validates payload begins b'PAR1'.
ilostat.open_question: TOC n.records can shrink/restate (not just grow) on revisions; decide whether to also re-pull ids whose count CHANGED (not only increased) to catch upstream restatements.

imf_commodity.strategy_reason: Small whole table (~1,236 PCPS series) that a single full re-pull rebuilds correctly; just drop the exists-guard and overwrite atomically when a DBnomics vintage signal moves.
imf_commodity.vintage_signal: [HISTORICAL - DBnomics BANNED R251] dataset metadata at api.db.nomics.world/v22 for IMF/PCPS (dataset-level indexed_at/converted_at, or num_found / nb_series); gate the overwrite on a change vs the value stored at last successful run.
imf_commodity.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/imf_commodity/imf_commodity.parquet (companion _log/_err are run logs, not data).
imf_commodity.rate_note: No key (DBnomics v22). 1.0s sleep/page, PAGE_SIZE=1000 series/page, 3-retry backoff; DBnomics fair-use applies. Write atomically (temp+rename) to avoid the corrupt-then-skipped-by-guard hazard.

imf_dbnomics.strategy_reason: Parameterized per dataset (IFS/DOT/BOP/...) with no since filter on DBnomics v22; DOT/BOP are LARGE so unconditional overwrite is wasteful — gate a whole-dataset re-download on a DBnomics dataset vintage signal and rebuild only changed datasets.
imf_dbnomics.vintage_signal: [HISTORICAL - DBnomics BANNED R251] dataset endpoint api.db.nomics.world/v22 for each provider/dataset (e.g. IMF/IFS, IMF/DOT, IMF/BOP): compare dataset indexed_at/converted_at (or nb_series/num_found) against a stored per-dataset value; re-pull+overwrite only when it advances.
imf_dbnomics.out_paths_note: Multi-dir: one single parquet per dataset ARG, data/clean_full/<dir>/<dir>.parquet where dir=imf_<code> for IMF (imf_ifs, imf_dot, imf_bop) or <provider>_<code> for others (e.g. undp_hdr). Also leaves a stale <file>.parquet.checkpoint that must be cleaned.
imf_dbnomics.rate_note: No key (DBnomics v22). PAGE_SIZE=1000, sleep 1.5s/page, timeout 300s, 4-retry backoff. DOT/BOP are long under fair-use. NB: the .checkpoint is written but never read on resume, so a killed run restarts at offset 0.
imf_dbnomics.open_question: Confirm the exact set of dataset args operationally scheduled (IFS/DOT/BOP only, or more) so each gets its own per-dataset vintage gate and output dir; and whether checkpoint-resume should be wired before enabling auto refresh of DOT/BOP.

imf_fsi.strategy_reason: The IMF SDMX GetData endpoint supports startPeriod/endPeriod, so read max(obs_date) from the parquet and fetch only newer periods, then merge — also fixes the hard-coded endPeriod=2025 truncation by parameterizing the window to the current year.
imf_fsi.vintage_signal: Date-tail always-fetch: each run sets startPeriod=last_obs_year and endPeriod=current_year against data.imf.org SDMX GetData (BI), merging any newer periods; no separate manifest needed because the date filter itself bounds the pull.
imf_fsi.since_param: startPeriod (with endPeriod set to current year; currently hard-coded 2000/2025 at lines 145 & 158 and must be parameterized)
