imf_fsi.rate_note: No key. Primary IMF SDMX data.imf.org/api/SDMX/BI; fallbacks data.imf.org/api/v1 and DBnomics IMF/FSI. RATE=0.5; 429 -> 60s sleep. Primary SDMX bulk endpoint is historically flaky (multi-fallback chain).
imf_fsi.open_question: series_key shape differs between the SDMX path (FSI:<indicator>:<country>) and the DBnomics fallback (FSI:<series_code>); pin the merge to a single source/key format so a fallback run does not fork keys and break the date-merge/downstream joins.

imf.strategy_reason: IMF SDMX 2.1 but the server supports no c[DIM] component filtering or Range resume and queries pull 'all' with no usable per-dataflow last-modified; practical refresh is re-pulling whole CHANGED dataflows, with the re-enumerated catalog as the change feed for new flows. Not S4 — IMF is not one of the four designated giants (statcan/oecd/eurostat/sdmx_nso).
imf.vintage_signal: Poll api.imf.org SDMX /dataflow each run (already done) -> _catalog.json: new base dataflows auto-detected; for change in existing flows, compare dataflow/DSD version+annotations (and the 91 *_VINTAGE re-release flows) vs _manifest.json, and rebuild only flows whose version advanced.
imf.out_paths_note: Multi-file (~767): data/clean_full/imf/<DID>.parquet for simple flows; giants split to <DID>__<FREQ>.parquet and MEGA cubes to <DID>__<FREQ>__<VAL>.parquet; state in data/clean_full/imf/_manifest.json and _catalog.json. Watch the freq-only vs sub-split double-count hazard when a flow moves in/out of MEGA between runs.
imf.rate_note: No key (api.imf.org/external/sdmx/2.1, SDMX-CSV mandatory — JSON/SDMX-ML broken server-side). 5-retry backoff, 600-900s timeouts. Host periodically OOM-kills concurrent ingest — keep requests small/restart-safe; use --skip-existing for resume.
imf.open_question: IMF /dataflow may not expose a reliable per-dataflow version/last-modified that advances on data revisions; need to confirm a change signal (else fall back to a scheduled periodic full re-pull, or adopt startPeriod=last_obs_year per-dataflow delta as a larger rewrite). Also decide whether to ingest the 91 *_VINTAGE flows (--vintages).

imf_weo.strategy_reason: DataMapper serves whole country x year matrices per indicator with no since filter; WEO is fully re-estimated each release, so a full re-pull rebuilds the single medium file correctly — drop the existence guard and overwrite when a new WEO edition is detected.
imf_weo.vintage_signal: Poll IMF DataMapper for the WEO release/edition tag (Apr & Oct rounds) — the code currently ignores the edition tag; surface it and overwrite only when the edition advances; otherwise a blind full re-pull + diff against existing parquet.
imf_weo.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/imf_weo/imf_weo.parquet (~588,836 rows; series_key '{indicator}:{country}', annual obs dated Dec 31).
imf_weo.rate_note: No key. Public IMF DataMapper; self-imposed RATE=0.5s across ~132 indicator GETs; 429 -> 60s sleep; UA carries admin@hfdatalibrary.com. No temp+rename — add atomic write since the in-place overwrite can leave a corrupt/absent file on mid-write crash.
imf_weo.open_question: WEO releases twice yearly (Apr/Oct), so the normalized cadence is 'irregular' rather than monthly — confirm an every-other-month or post-release poll schedule, and whether DataMapper exposes a stable edition tag to gate on (vs blind re-pull).

ine_spain.strategy_reason: The wstempus DATOS_TABLA endpoint supports an nult=N (last-N periods) / date-filtered variant, so read max(obs_date) per (table,cod) from the op parquet, fetch only recent periods, and merge-dedup into the per-op file instead of the current all-or-nothing skip.
ine_spain.vintage_signal: Date-tail fetch via DATOS_TABLA nult=N (or date filter); each table's records carry Fecha (unix-ms)/Anyo, so request recent periods and merge anything newer than stored max(obs_date) per (table,cod). New operations still picked up via OPERACIONES_DISPONIBLES enumeration.
ine_spain.since_param: nult (last-N periods on DATOS_TABLA; or the date-filtered DATOS_TABLA variant keyed on Fecha)
ine_spain.out_paths_note: Multi-file: one parquet per operation, data/clean_full/ine_spain/op_{op_id}.parquet (~99 files incl. _ine_spain_log.txt; series_key 'table={id}:cod={cod}:nombre={name}'; largest ~25MB op_197).
ine_spain.rate_note: No key. RATE=0.3s between table GETs; 429 -> 60s sleep. Oversized ops (e.g. 353 Atlas de renta, 540) are buffered whole-in-memory and can OOM/stall — deferrable via env INE_SKIP_OPS, which leaves them as a tracked gap.
ine_spain.key_env: INE_SKIP_OPS (optional, to defer oversized ops; not a credential)
ine_spain.open_question: Verify nult/date-filter is supported on the bulk DATOS_TABLA path used here (not only on per-series endpoints); if not, fall back to per-op bulk_snapshot_if_changed gated on a table-level vintage. Also resolve how the deferred INE_SKIP_OPS ops get collected so they aren't a permanent gap.

insee_bdm.strategy_reason: INSEE BDM is SDMX 2.1 (api.insee.fr/series/BDM/V1) and the profile confirms data/{FLOW_ID} accepts updatedAfter + startPeriod/lastNObservations; pull only obs newer than last_obs per dataflow and merge.
insee_bdm.vintage_signal: Per-dataflow change detection via GET data/{FLOW_ID}?updatedAfter=<last_success_timestamp>; enumerate the ~243 flow ids from the dataflow/all/all/latest catalog. No global manifest.
insee_bdm.since_param: startPeriod=<max(obs_date)+1 period> on data/{FLOW_ID} (use updatedAfter=<last_success ISO datetime> to gate which flows changed).
insee_bdm.out_paths_note: Multi-file: one parquet per dataflow at data/clean_full/insee_bdm/{FLOW_ID}.parquet (~201-243 files). Merge per flow by read+concat+dedup on (idbank,obs_date); add .tmp staging since current writer has no atomic write.
insee_bdm.rate_note: No API key (public, Accept: application/xml). 0.5s between flows; HTTP 429 -> 30s*(attempt+1) backoff. No declared per-minute cap.

insee_melodi.strategy_reason: Melodi /data/{FLOW_CODE} supports startPeriod/lastNObservations and the catalog exposes a per-dataflow lastUpdate; gate on lastUpdate and pull startPeriod=last_obs+1 per flow rather than re-paginating all flows.
insee_melodi.vintage_signal: Catalog lastUpdate field per dataflow (dataflow/all catalog) compared against a stored per-flow marker; enumerate ~109 flow codes from that catalog.
insee_melodi.since_param: startPeriod=<max(obs_date)+1 period> on /data/{FLOW_CODE} (gated by catalog lastUpdate > stored marker).
insee_melodi.out_paths_note: Multi-file: one parquet per dataflow at data/clean_full/insee_melodi/{FLOW_CODE}.parquet (~79 files). Merge by read+concat+dedup on (flow,series_key,obs_date); some flows large (DS_BPE* ~25 MB). Add .tmp staging (no atomic write today).
insee_melodi.rate_note: No API key (keyless 'libre' plan, Accept: application/json). Documented 30 req/min cap -> RATE_DELAY 2.1s between pages/flows; HTTP 429 -> 60s sleep.

insee_sirene.strategy_reason: The on-disk source is populated by ingest_insee_sirene_bulk.py (the API script is NOT the populator): 6 whole-registry Stock parquet files republished monthly via data.gouv.fr with no date param; gate on resource last_modified/filesize and re-download+rebuild only changed files.
insee_sirene.vintage_signal: data.gouv.fr dataset 5b7ffc618b4c4169d30727e0 API resources[].last_modified and resources[].filesize per Stock file, compared to local file mtime/size; download+overwrite only when changed (current code only checks local existence -> staleness trap).
insee_sirene.out_paths_note: Multi-file but FIXED set: 6 files under data/clean_full/insee_sirene/ (StockUniteLegale, StockEtablissement, StockUniteLegaleHistorique, StockEtablissementHistorique, StockEtablissementLiensSuccession, StockDoublons; ~4.6 GB on disk, ~7 GB download). Replace per-file atomically; avoid mixing vintages by refreshing all changed files together.
insee_sirene.rate_note: No API key (public data.gouv.fr). Streaming download with HTTP Range resume via .part, 5 retries 10s*(attempt+1) backoff, 600s socket timeout; no rate limit; large bandwidth/disk footprint.
insee_sirene.key_env: none (bulk path). NOTE: the sibling API script ingest_insee_sirene.py requires INSEE_SIRENE_KEY but is not the populator.
insee_sirene.open_question: Two scripts map to this source_id: keep the bulk script as the populator (S5). The API script (ingest_insee_sirene.py) hits a HARD offset=10000 ceiling and can only ever return ~10k records -- it cannot serve as a delta path and should not be wired into the update system; confirm it is deprecated/retired for this source.

ipea.strategy_reason: IPEA OData4 ValoresSerie accepts a server-side date filter ($filter=VALDATA gt {date}); fetch only obs newer than per-series max(obs_date) and append, instead of the current skip-if-series-key-present rule that never extends existing series.
ipea.vintage_signal: Date-tail per series: compute max(obs_date) per series_key from existing parquet and request ValoresSerie with $filter=VALDATA gt {max}. New series picked up from the freshly fetched Metadados active-series list (SERSTATUS='A'). No single upstream manifest/last-modified.
ipea.since_param: $filter=VALDATA gt {max(obs_date) per series_key} on the IPEA OData4 ValoresSerie endpoint.
ipea.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/ipea/ipea.parquet (~622k rows; schema series_key,obs_date,value; series_key = SERCODIGO or SERCODIGO:TERCODIGO). Dedup on (series_key,obs_date). CRITICAL: current checkpoint writes pq.write_table directly over the file (no .tmp/os.replace) -- add atomic write before enabling incremental to avoid corrupting the single output.
ipea.rate_note: No API key (public ipeadata.gov.br OData4, plain http://). RATE 0.3s between series GETs; HTTP 429 -> 60s sleep; 3 retries.

irena.strategy_reason: Two PxWeb scripts (ingest_irena.py + ingest_irena_country.py) producing many tiny per-table parquets; tables are vintage-stamped (H1/H2) and re-published whole, no usable date delta -- gate on the catalog crawl surfacing a new/changed table id and overwrite the affected table parquet.
irena.vintage_signal: BFS catalog crawl of IRENASTAT + RE-STAT for new/changed table ids (e.g. *_2026_H2_*); for ingest_irena_country.py the table ids are HARD-CODED in LARGE_TABLES (lines 18-26) so new vintages need a manual id bump. No HEAD/Last-Modified per file. Revisions to an existing id are missed unless the table is overwritten.
irena.out_paths_note: Both scripts write to the SAME dir data/clean_full/irena/: ingest_irena.py -> {tableid}.parquet (crawled, ~4 small files), ingest_irena_country.py -> ctry_{safe}.parquet (~3 files). Overwrite changed/new-vintage tables; PRUNE orphan superseded-vintage parquets on H1->H2 bumps (they otherwise accumulate). Watch ingest_irena_country.py's silent partial-table bake (failed batch dropped, file still written).
irena.rate_note: No API key (PxWeb public, CC BY 4.0). Self-throttled RATE 1.0s + 0.3s/catalog item (main) and 0.5s/batch + 1s/table (country); 429 not specially handled -> add 429 backoff. Country script needs the 20-at-a-time POST batching because full-table POSTs 400/500.
irena.open_question: ingest_irena_country.py uses a hard-coded LARGE_TABLES vintage map with no catalog crawl, so new H1/H2 vintages won't be auto-detected for those 3 country tables -- decide whether to add a crawl/alert or accept manual id bumps (semiannual). Also decide an orphan-vintage pruning policy.

istat.strategy_reason: ISTAT is SDMX REST (sdmx.istat.it + esploradati.istat.it) and startPeriod is already plumbed through build_data_url; set the per-flow window lower bound to max(obs_date) on disk, fetch only newer windows, and merge (the existing _accumulate last-write-wins dedup supports safe overlap).
istat.vintage_signal: New flow id appearing in the union catalog (get_dataflows) signals new flows; for revisions to existing flows there is no updatedAfter exposed here, so use a date-tail per flow: startPeriod = year of max(obs_date) on disk and re-sweep forward. No global manifest.
istat.since_param: startPeriod=<year of max(obs_date) per flow> via build_data_url (decade/year windowing); endPeriod walks to present.
istat.out_paths_note: Multi-file: per-flow parquet in data/clean_full/istat/ (~755 files). SHARED dir+filename convention with ingest_sdmx_nso.py -- the two jobs dedupe via skip-existing; a careless *.parquet delete affects both. Switch write_flow from overwrite to merge-with-existing on (series_key,obs_date). Checkpoints _sliced_done.json/_sliced_unrecoverable.json are atomic.
istat.rate_note: No API key. Two hosts: sdmx.istat.it (fast) + esploradati.istat.it (chronically slow/flaky). RATE 1.5s, TIMEOUT 300s, RETRIES 5, 429 -> 60s; MAX_SIZE 500MB triggers subdivision. If both hosts down the run aborts (expects a watcher relaunch).
istat.open_question: This is a completion/recovery pass over the main ISTAT sweep (ingest_sdmx_nso.py) sharing one output dir. Confirm the delta/merge is implemented in the primary sdmx_nso job and this sliced script stays a recovery tool, so the two don't fight over overwrite-vs-merge semantics. Also note --only mode intentionally OVERWRITES a flow (data-loss risk if a flaky host returns a smaller subset than the prior file).

kof_globalization.strategy_reason: Single tiny annual XLSX with no per-observation API and re-estimated each yearly edition; the correct pattern is full overwrite when a new edition appears -- gate on the year-stamped URL/edition signal rather than blind re-download. Not S6: a hardcoded URL is auto-fetchable.
kof_globalization.vintage_signal: Probe for a new year-stamped edition: HEAD/GET the ethz.ch dam URL for the next year (e.g. KOFGI_2026_public.xlsx) or parse the KOF download page; current KOF_URLS (lines 31-38) hard-codes year URLs tried in order, first >5000 bytes wins. No Last-Modified delta on the existing file is needed -- edition = new URL.
kof_globalization.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/kof_globalization/kof_globalization.parquet (~1.4 MB; series_key KOF:{index}:{ISO}, annual Dec-31 obs). Overwrite atomically on a new edition.
kof_globalization.rate_note: No API key (free for academic use). fetch() only 2 attempts, requires >5000 bytes, treats 403/404 as give-up-this-URL.
kof_globalization.open_question: URL-rot: dam paths change between editions and a failed probe silently no-ops ('All KOF URLs failed') leaving stale data without erroring -- the edition-probe must alert a human when the new-year URL can't be resolved. Parser also takes the FIRST sheet yielding obs (line 143); confirm sheet order is stable across editions.

ksh.strategy_reason: KSH STADAT per-theme CSVs are full presentation tables with no since param but tiny; re-pull the small CSVs and overwrite/upsert per theme when the published TOC changes, rather than the current theme-level skip-if-exists that misses revisions.
ksh.vintage_signal: KSH STADAT TOC/release-calendar signal: the sibling ingest_ksh_stadat.py reads toc.json (which this script does NOT) -- use toc.json (and/or per-table Last-Modified) to detect which themes changed, then re-fetch+overwrite those theme CSVs. This plain-UA script currently has no vintage probe at all.
ksh.out_paths_note: Multi-file: per-theme parquet in data/clean_full/ksh/ (~25 files; series_key KSH:{theme}{NNNN}:..., annual Dec-31 only). Upsert per theme on (series_key,obs_date) instead of all-or-nothing skip. Note this script is superseded in practice by ingest_ksh_stadat.py which writes a DIFFERENT output dir and keeps sub-annual periods.
ksh.rate_note: No declared API key but KSH runs an F5 WAF that rejects minimal clients: this script's plain library UA is WAF-exposed and may be throttled/blocked (handles 429 by 30s sleep but not the 200 'Request Rejected' WAF page). RATE 0.3s. The sibling stadat script sends full browser headers to pass the WAF.
ksh.open_question: F5 WAF: keep this source auto-fetchable (S1) ONLY if it adopts the sibling's full browser headers; with the current plain UA it risks hard WAF blocking, which would push it to S6 (manual_vintage). Decide whether to retire ingest_ksh_hungary.py in favor of ingest_ksh_stadat.py (more complete, reads toc.json, WAF-safe headers, sub-annual obs) as the populator for this source.

ksh_stadat.strategy_reason: Catalog-driven (~1,632 STADAT tables) full-table CSV pulls with NO since param; gate on the toc.json catalog + per-table change and rebuild only changed theme files.
ksh_stadat.vintage_signal: Always re-fetch toc.json and diff its contents against cached _catalog.json to catch new/changed tables; no per-table Last-Modified header exists, so re-pull a theme's CSVs and upsert when toc entries change.
ksh_stadat.out_paths_note: Writes 27 per-theme parquet files under data/clean_full/ksh_stadat/ (per-theme skip-if-exists) plus cached _catalog.json (~1.1MB). Multi-file, theme-granular.
ksh_stadat.rate_note: F5 WAF blocker handled in-code (browser headers required, NOT library UA; escalating WAF_SLEEPS=[60,120,300,600,900]s, 12-attempt get_bytes, main aborts after 3 consecutive WAF losses). RATE=1.2s + 0-0.8s jitter. No API key.
ksh_stadat.open_question: WAF means partial/slow crawls are normal — should a changed-toc rebuild be allowed to span multiple runs (resume at theme granularity), and is full toc re-diff acceptable given the WAF cost, or should we cap how many themes refresh per run?

maddison.strategy_reason: Single static historical XLSX behind a hardcoded URL with no date param; correct refresh is re-download+rebuild only when a new edition ships, gated on the file's vintage signal.
maddison.vintage_signal: HEAD Last-Modified / Content-Length on the mpd2020.xlsx primary URL (and the Dataverse datafile/421302 2023 fallback); re-download+overwrite only when the header changes.
maddison.out_paths_note: Single file data/clean_full/maddison/maddison.parquet (~208KB), skip-if-exists. NOTE: a separate ingester jobs/ingest_ggdc.py also produces Maddison output to its own path — keep the two from colliding.
maddison.rate_note: No API key (CC BY 4.0, direct XLSX), 300s timeout. Writes nothing if both URLs fail.
maddison.open_question: The 2020 primary URL is preferred over the newer 2023 Dataverse edition, so refresh keeps the OLDER edition unless URLS is reordered — should we flip the priority / add the 2023 (or later mpd2025) edition as primary so the vintage check tracks the newest release?

nasa_giss.strategy_reason: Tiny single-file table rebuilt wholesale from 4 full wide GISTEMP CSVs re-published monthly (no date-windowed endpoint); just gate on a vintage header and overwrite atomically.
nasa_giss.vintage_signal: HTTP Last-Modified header on the GISTEMP CSVs (GLB/NH/SH/ZonAnn .Ts+dSST.csv at data.giss.nasa.gov); if any CSV's Last-Modified advanced, re-download all 4 and overwrite. Data is trivially cheap, so unconditional monthly overwrite is also acceptable.
nasa_giss.out_paths_note: Single file data/clean_full/nasa_giss/giss_temp.parquet (~28KB). Current os.path.exists early-return guard (lines 136-138) must be removed/bypassed so re-runs actually refresh.
nasa_giss.rate_note: No API key, plain requests.get 30s timeout, custom UA, sequential per-file GETs. No rate limit.

nbp.strategy_reason: NBP API natively supports a server-side date-range path; fetch only obs newer than each currency's stored last_obs_date and append/merge.
nbp.vintage_signal: Date-tail always-fetch: per currency, compute max(obs_date) from nbp.parquet and request the tail; weekends/holidays simply return empty.
nbp.since_param: {start} path segment in /rates/{table}/{code}/{start}/{end} (= per-series max(obs_date)+1 day; honor the 367-day-per-request cap via chunking).
nbp.out_paths_note: Single file data/clean_full/nbp/nbp.parquet (~1.5MB), checkpoint-overwritten every 5 series during the run. Replace whole-history-per-series skip with per-series since + dedup on (series_key, obs_date).
nbp.rate_note: No API key (api.nbp.pl open). Self-throttled RATE=0.5s/series, 0.2s/chunk; 429 -> 30s sleep, 3 retries; max 367 days/request.

noaa.strategy_reason: Bulk per-station GSOM/GSOY CSV archive (~214K files) with NO date param; gate each station file on Last-Modified, re-download only changed stations, then full --build to rebuild shards.
noaa.vintage_signal: Per-station conditional GET (If-Modified-Since / compare Last-Modified header vs cached CSV mtime) against the NCEI bulk archive; re-download stations whose header advanced. Also re-run --enumerate to detect new stations.
noaa.out_paths_note: Multi-file: data/clean_full/noaa/<ds>__<PREFIX>.parquet + <ds>__<PREFIX>__series.parquet for ds in {gsom,gsoy} (~834 parquet files, ~552M obs). Raw cache data/raw/noaa/{gsom,gsoy}/*.csv (~214K CSVs) + manifests must also be refreshed. Build is idempotent (per-shard ParquetWriter overwrite).
noaa.rate_note: No API key (NCEI public domain). Scale/rate is the blocker: ~214K CSVs, workers capped 1..6, Retry session backoff on 429/5xx; build single-threaded. refresh_cost=large.
noaa.open_question: Does NCEI emit reliable per-file Last-Modified on the GSOM/GSOY station CSVs? If not, the only fresh-detection option is periodic full re-download of the archive (expensive) or a published manifest — needs confirmation before relying on conditional GET.

norgesbank.strategy_reason: Norges Bank is SDMX (SDMX-JSON) and supports startPeriod/endPeriod; pull per-dataflow delta from last_obs+1 and merge instead of whole-flow-or-nothing.
norgesbank.vintage_signal: SDMX startPeriod windowed re-fetch per flow (no updatedAfter on this API); request startPeriod=last_obs+1 and append. Always-fetch the short tail per flow as the freshness probe.
norgesbank.out_paths_note: Single combined file data/clean_full/norgesbank/norgesbank.parquet (~12MB, 10 dataflows). WARNING: sibling per-dataflow files (EXR.parquet, IR.parquet, ANN_FX_SPU.parquet, MONEY_MARKET.parquet, etc.) in the same dir come from a DIFFERENT/older ingester and are NOT touched by this script — downstream globbing could double-count.
norgesbank.rate_note: No API key (data.norges-bank.no open). Self-throttled RATE=1.0s/flow, 120s timeout, 3 retries (5s*(attempt+1) backoff); 400/404 treated as empty. Only 10 flows.
norgesbank.open_question: Should the legacy per-dataflow sibling parquet files (from the other ingester) be removed/deprecated so the combined norgesbank.parquet is the single source, avoiding duplicate ingestion downstream?

nyfed.strategy_reason: Fetched via FRED, which exposes a server-side observation_start date filter; derive it from each series' stored max(obs_date) and pull only the tail.
nyfed.vintage_signal: Date-tail always-fetch via FRED observation_start; per series compute max(obs_date) from {name}.parquet and request from there (data tiny — full overwrite also fine).
nyfed.since_param: observation_start=<max(obs_date) (or +1 day)> on the FRED series/observations call (currently hardcoded 2000-01-01).
nyfed.out_paths_note: Multi-file, one parquet per logical series: data/clean_full/nyfed/<name>.parquet for sofr,tgcr,obfr,sofr30d/90d/180d,sofridx,tgcrvol (~8 files). NOTE: duplicate 'tgcr' dict key drops the non-RATE TGCR variant (latent coverage bug); bgcr intentionally absent (unavailable via FRED).
nyfed.rate_note: REQUIRES FRED_API_KEY (.env via core.config.load_env; SystemExit if missing). FRED public rate limits; self-throttles 1s between series.
nyfed.open_question: Confirm the duplicate 'tgcr' key should be fixed (currently only TGCRRATE is fetched, the TGCR variant is silently dropped) — coverage decision for a human.

oecd.strategy_reason: OECD is one of the 4 designated giants (~1,413 dataflows, ~6.0B obs, ~57GB); refresh only whole CHANGED dataflows via the catalog change-feed rather than re-pulling everything.
oecd.vintage_signal: OECD SDMX catalog as change-feed: re-download the catalog (--catalog -> data/raw/oecd/manifest.json + dataflows_all.xml, ~1509 flows) and diff per-flow last-updated/annotations to select changed dataflows to re-pull. (Per-flow SDMX startPeriod could refine within a changed flow, but selection is unit-level per the giants strategy.)
oecd.since_param: n/a (giant strategy refreshes whole changed units; optionally startPeriod=YYYY-MM on /rest/data/.../all within a changed flow)
oecd.out_paths_note: Multi-file, one parquet per dataflow: data/clean_full/oecd/<AGENCY>__<DATAFLOW_ID>.parquet (~1,413 files). 'partial' flows (failed REF_AREA/COUNTERPART splits) get skipped forever by resume — must be force-cleared to repair, so the changed-unit selector must also re-pull partials.
oecd.rate_note: No API key (CC BY 4.0) but Cloudflare + app-level download quota: HTTP 429 'exceeded number of requests' -> 35s global cooldown; global token-bucket MIN_INTERVAL default 4.0s (env OECD_MIN_INTERVAL); default workers=2. Full re-pull is many hours — the whole point of changed-units. refresh_cost=giant.
oecd.open_question: Does the OECD catalog (manifest.json/dataflows_all.xml) expose a reliable per-dataflow last-updated timestamp to drive change detection? If not, changed-unit selection has no clean signal and we'd fall back to periodic full or startPeriod-tail per flow — needs confirmation.

ofr.strategy_reason: OFR v1/series/dataset endpoint accepts a server-side &mindate=YYYY-MM-DD date filter, so fetch only obs newer than stored max(obs_date) per dataset and merge/de-dup.
ofr.vintage_signal: date-tail always-fetch: read max(obs_date) from each existing {ds}.parquet and pass it as &mindate; daily rates/repo/MMF move daily so always poll with the date tail rather than gating on a separate signal.
ofr.since_param: &mindate=YYYY-MM-DD appended to GET data.financialresearch.gov/v1/series/dataset?dataset=<key> (value = stored max obs_date per dataset, ideally last_obs+1 day).
ofr.out_paths_note: Writes one parquet per dataset to data/clean_full/ofr/{fnyr,repo,mmf,nypd}.parquet (4 files, ~425K obs). Track last_obs_date per dataset; merge+de-dup on (series_id,obs_date,dataset). Must remove the current existence-skip guard (lines 51-54) which otherwise no-ops re-runs.
ofr.rate_note: No API key (US public domain). Self-throttle time.sleep(0.5) between datasets, 120s timeout; non-200 logged and skipped with no retry, self-heals next run.
ofr.open_question: Confirm the OFR endpoint actually honors &mindate (matrix asserts it but the current code never sends it); if not honored, fall back to unconditional full re-pull+overwrite (data is small).

ons_uk.strategy_reason: ONS beta API has no observation-level since filter; it serves a whole-version CSV per dataset, so the only feasible refresh is a version-gated full re-download of changed datasets.
ons_uk.vintage_signal: GET https://api.beta.ons.gov.uk/v1/datasets/<id> and read links.latest_version.id (version number); store it in a sidecar and re-download the dataset's version CSV only when it changed. Catalog walk /v1/datasets also surfaces brand-new datasets.
ons_uk.out_paths_note: One parquet per dataset: data/clean_full/ons_uk/<dataset_id>.parquet (42 files). Whole-CSV rebuild per changed dataset; --only=cpih01,lfst01 can scope the catalog. Must replace the os.path.exists skip (lines 124-128) with a version comparison.
ons_uk.rate_note: No API key (OGL v3.0). Self-imposed RATE=0.5s between catalog pages and datasets; 429 handled with 60s sleep. UA carries a hfdatalibrary contact email.
ons_uk.open_question: Confirm links.latest_version.id is the right per-dataset vintage field to gate on (vs an edition/release-date field); also decide atomic temp-rename writes since current writes are not atomic.

owid.strategy_reason: OWID grapher CSV (csvType=full) exposes no per-observation since; only feasible incremental is HEAD-ETag/Last-Modified gating per chart and re-downloading whole changed charts; sitemap manifest surfaces new slugs.
owid.vintage_signal: Per-slug HTTP ETag/Last-Modified via HEAD on each chart's .csv URL (store in a manifest, re-pull only when changed); plus the sitemap manifest https://ourworldindata.org/sitemap.xml (cached to data/raw/owid/owid_slugs.txt) for NEW chart slugs, refreshed with --enumerate.
owid.out_paths_note: One parquet per chart slug: data/clean_full/owid/<slug>.parquet (~3,786 files) plus _ingest_summary.json; raw cache data/raw/owid/owid_slugs.txt + owid_sitemap.xml. Must replace the blind skip_existing (lines 273-279) with an ETag comparison.
owid.rate_note: No API key (CC BY 4.0), polite UA; workers capped at 6; exponential backoff on 429/5xx. HTTP 403 = non-redistributable third-party charts (excluded by design, not an error). Atomic writes already in place.
owid.open_question: Verify the OWID grapher CSV endpoint returns a stable ETag/Last-Modified on HEAD; if it does not, fall back to content-hash diffing or periodic full re-pull of all slugs.

oxcgrt.strategy_reason: Closed single-file dataset (Jan 2020-Dec 2022) from a fixed GitHub raw CSV with no date param; small whole table best handled by a vintage-gated atomic overwrite.
oxcgrt.vintage_signal: GitHub commit SHA / raw Last-Modified on the OxCGRT raw CSV (HEAD the first reachable of the 3 candidate raw.githubusercontent URLs, or query the GitHub commits API for the file path); only rebuild if it moved. In practice the project ended, so this will essentially never fire.
oxcgrt.out_paths_note: Single file data/clean_full/oxcgrt/oxcgrt.parquet plus _oxcgrt_log.txt/_oxcgrt_err.txt. Currently main() no-ops if the file exists. WARNING: forced rebuild streams ParquetWriter directly to the final path (non-atomic) so a mid-run crash leaves a truncated parquet — write to temp+rename if wiring real refreshes.
oxcgrt.rate_note: No API key (CC BY 4.0, Oxford via GitHub raw); 2s sleep between the 3 candidate URLs, single GET each (no retry). File must be >10,000 bytes to be accepted.
oxcgrt.open_question: Confirm OxCGRT is truly frozen (project ended Dec 2022); if so this can be treated as a one-time static load needing no scheduled poll at all.

penn_world_table.strategy_reason: Whole annual panel republished as one Excel workbook per version (with back-revisions), and the script already full-overwrites all 42 variable parquets each run — gate that on a Dataverse vintage signal so it only re-runs when the release changes.
penn_world_table.vintage_signal: Dataverse datafile id / version for pwt110.xlsx (current datafile id 554105) — compare the upstream datafile id or dataset version metadata before downloading; bump PWT_VERSION + DATA_URL constants on a new release.
penn_world_table.out_paths_note: One parquet per VARIABLE: data/clean_full/penn_world_table/<variable>.parquet (42 files) plus _ingest_summary.json; raw workbook cached at data/raw/penn_world_table/pwt110.xlsx. Atomic per-file overwrite already implemented. Distinct from the legacy 'pwt' source (PWT 10.0).
penn_world_table.rate_note: No API key (CC BY 4.0). Single GET to dataverse.nl with 5-try exponential backoff (1/2/4/8/16s); no rate concerns (one file). Needs openpyxl+pandas. Hard guard raises on a column missing a VAR_DEFS legend entry (schema-drift tripwire).
penn_world_table.open_question: A new PWT vintage with renamed/added columns will RAISE (missing_def guard) — confirm a human updates VAR_DEFS + PWT_VERSION/DATA_URL when version 11.x/12.0 drops; should vintage detection auto-alert on the Dataverse version bump?

pip.strategy_reason: World Bank PIP REST has no observation-level since (queries are country=all/year=all); the single parquet is re-estimated per release, so gate the full rebuild on the PIP version catalog and overwrite atomically when the vintage changes.
pip.vintage_signal: PIP version catalog: GET api.worldbank.org/pip/v1/versions and record the current data vintage string; rebuild only when it changes (replace the top-of-main existence skip at lines 65-67 with a vintage comparison).
pip.out_paths_note: Single file data/clean_full/pip/pip.parquet plus _pip_log.txt/_pip_err.txt. Rebuild = 10 bulk calls (one per poverty line in POV_LINES), each all-countries x all-years. WARNING: streaming ParquetWriter writes directly to the final path (non-atomic) — a crashed force-refresh leaves a partial parquet the next run skips; write temp+rename.
pip.rate_note: No API key (CC BY 4.0, World Bank). RATE=1.0s between poverty-line calls; 429 handled with 30s sleep. reporting_level='national', welfare_type='all', fill_gaps='false'.
pip.open_question: Confirm the exact field in /pip/v1/versions to use as the vintage key (release version vs ppp_year vs published date), and note distributional indicators are duplicated across povline labels by design (inflates obs count).

pwt.strategy_reason: Legacy PWT 10.0 single-workbook bulk download with no since filter; a small whole table re-estimated per vintage — gate on the rug.nl file vintage and atomically overwrite. (Superseded by penn_world_table.)
pwt.vintage_signal: HTTP Last-Modified / ETag on https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/docs/pwt100.xlsx (HEAD before the cheap full rebuild). PWT 10.0 is a frozen vintage so this will essentially never change.
pwt.out_paths_note: Single file data/clean_full/pwt/pwt.parquet (note series_key uses ':' separator, unlike penn_world_table's '|'); no raw cache, no summary json. main() no-ops if the file exists. SuperSEDED by jobs/ingest_penn_world_table.py (PWT 11.0) which writes a DIFFERENT dir — these are two distinct source_ids/dirs covering overlapping data.
pwt.rate_note: No API key (CC BY 4.0). Single GET to rug.nl, 300s timeout, NO retry/backoff (one attempt). Needs openpyxl. write_table to final path only after a fully successful parse (failure leaves prior file intact).
pwt.open_question: RECOMMEND RETIRING this legacy 10.0 script in favor of penn_world_table (11.0) — confirm with a human whether to keep the frozen 10.0 vintage live or deprecate it to avoid duplicated-effort/two-dir confusion.

pxweb.strategy_reason: PxWeb data POST selects explicit per-dimension value lists with no date cutoff, but table metadata exposes an 'updated' timestamp — gate whole-table re-download on that timestamp (manifest-style change detection); the directory crawl surfaces new tables.
pxweb.vintage_signal: PxWeb per-table metadata 'updated' (last-updated) field from tableinfo/table meta — store it alongside each parquet and re-download only when the upstream timestamp is newer (replaces the blind os.path.exists skip at lines 161-164 / DST 329-332). Directory crawl (crawl_pxweb_tables; DST tables list) detects NEW tables.
pxweb.out_paths_note: MULTI-PROVIDER, multi-dir: one parquet per table under data/clean_full/<provider>/ for provider in {scb,ssb,statfin,dst,cso,bfs} (e.g. dst 705, ssb 186, statfin 135, scb 9, cso 44, bfs 1); 5-col schema provider/table_id/series_key/obs_date/value; DST files named DST__<id>.parquet; ssb/statfin also write _catalog.json. Large cross-products (>MAX_CELLS=50,000) are trimmed to the last 200 time periods, so those tables permanently hold only recent history unless re-pulled. Per-table writes are non-atomic.
pxweb.rate_note: No API keys. Per-provider rate: scb 0.5, ssb 1.0, statfin 1.0, dst 0.5, cso 1.0, bfs 2.0; 429 handled (30s*attempt). Quirks: SCB uses '/sv/' base (EN 400s), SSB tree starts at /table/; PxWeb rejects 'all'/'*' wildcards (explicit value lists sent); crawl depth capped at max_depth=8.
pxweb.open_question: Confirm every provider's PxWeb metadata reliably exposes the 'updated' timestamp; and decide whether MAX_CELLS-trimmed big tables need a periodic full re-pull (a trailing-200-period merge / read-modify-write would require code not currently present).

rba.strategy_reason: ~216 whole-history CSVs scraped from an HTML index, each a full dump with NO date param; cannot do a server-side since-delta, so detect changed CSVs via Last-Modified / the CSV 'Publication date' row and re-download+rebuild only those.
rba.vintage_signal: Scrape https://www.rba.gov.au/statistics/tables/ for /statistics/tables/csv/*.csv hrefs, then per-CSV gate on HTTP Last-Modified (or the in-file 'Publication date' metadata row) compared against a stored per-table state file; re-pull only tables whose signal moved.
rba.out_paths_note: Currently single file data/clean_full/rba/rba.parquet holding all ~216 tables; to make S5 effective, move to a per-table parquet layout so only changed tables rebuild (note: no in-run (key,date) dedup today — overlapping Series IDs across CSVs can dupe).
rba.rate_note: No key; RATE=0.5s between files, 4x retry, 60s sleep on 429, 120s timeout; link discovery depends on the HTML/href regex (site redesign breaks it).
rba.open_question: Does rba.gov.au serve a reliable per-CSV Last-Modified header, or must we always GET and parse the Publication-date row to detect change?

riksbank.strategy_reason: SWEA v1 API accepts a server-side date range so we can fetch only obs after the stored last_obs_date and merge; current skip-if-series-exists logic freezes daily series, so a true since-delta is the right fix.
riksbank.vintage_signal: Date-tail always-fetch: for each series request observations after the stored last obs_date; also periodically refresh _series_catalog.json (GET /Series) to detect newly-added series rather than reusing the cache.
riksbank.since_param: URL path /swea/v1/Observations/{seriesId}/{from}/{to} where from = stored last_obs_date+1, to = today (or catalog observationMaxDate).
riksbank.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/riksbank/riksbank.parquet (~2.3 MB; key 'RIKSBANK:<seriesId>'), plus sidecar _series_catalog.json and _riksbank_log.txt. One dir; add (key,date) dedup on append.
riksbank.rate_note: No key; api.riksbank.se aggressive limits — RATE=3.0s between obs calls, 8x retry, parses 'N seconds' from 429 body (default 65s); ~117 series so cold run is several minutes.
riksbank.open_question: Cached _series_catalog.json hides new Riksbank series — confirm an acceptable cadence for re-pulling the /Series catalog so new series aren't missed.

scb.strategy_reason: SCB is a PxWeb NSO whose table queries can restrict the time-variable selection to only new periods (PxWeb startPeriod-equivalent), so pull periods after the stored last period and merge per table/subject rather than full-pull.
scb.vintage_signal: Per-table: read PxWeb table metadata (time variable's available value list / updated field) and request only time codes > stored last code; refresh the BFS _catalog.json periodically instead of always reusing the cache, to catch new tables.
scb.since_param: PxWeb POST query 'time' dimension selection = value-list of periods after the stored last time code (filter=item with only new period codes), instead of selecting ALL time values.
scb.out_paths_note: Multi-file: one parquet per top-level subject area data/clean_full/scb/<SUBJ>.parquet (AA, AM, BE, BO, EN, FM, HA, HE, JO ...), plus _catalog.json and _scb_log.txt. Many units under one dir; note MAX_CELLS=100000 leaves oversized tables at partial (aggregate-only) coverage that incremental won't repair.
scb.rate_note: No key; api.scb.se PxWeb ~10 req/s limit, RATE=0.2s used; 3x retry, 30s sleep on 429; POST 400 when query exceeds cell cap (MAX_CELLS branch). Cold crawl is long.
scb.open_question: Does the SCB PxWeb metadata expose a reliable per-table last-updated field, or must we always request the latest period and diff to decide which tables changed? Also: how to backfill the MAX_CELLS partial-coverage tables under an incremental model.

sdmx_nso.strategy_reason: Named giant (one of statcan/oecd/eurostat/sdmx_nso) fronting the library's largest sources (eurostat 6.1B obs, ilostat 388M, bis); refresh only whole CHANGED dataflows via the SDMX change-feed rather than full multi-hour sweeps.
sdmx_nso.vintage_signal: SDMX ?updatedAfter=<last_success_timestamp> per provider/dataflow as the change-feed to identify changed flows; for change-confirmed flows re-pull (optionally bounded by ?startPeriod). Record per-flow last run time/max obs_date in a state file.
sdmx_nso.since_param: data/<agency>,<flow>/?updatedAfter=<last_success> to detect changed flows, then ?startPeriod=<last_obs+1> on the changed flow (startPeriod already used as a constant for ECB).
sdmx_nso.out_paths_note: Multi-dir, multi-file: one parquet per dataflow under data/clean_full/<out_key or provider>/<flow_id>.parquet across MANY provider dirs (istat, unicef, bundesbank, idb, adb, norgesbank, ksh, stats_nz, gus, stat_austria, insee_sdmx, bis, ilo, eurostat, ecb_sdmx). IMPORTANT: both 'istat' and 'istat_esploradati' write to data/clean_full/istat (shared dir); provider arg is mandatory and per-invocation (no global flag).
sdmx_nso.rate_note: No keys (all keyless); per-provider rate 1.0-2.0s and 180-600s timeouts; 4x retry, 60s on 429; XML flows >800 MB silently skipped (gaps); known flaky hosts (esploradati.istat.it, stat_austria, idb). SDMX_SKIP_FLOWS must be UNSET for completeness.
sdmx_nso.open_question: Which of the ~15 providers actually honor ?updatedAfter (coverage varies by provider) — those that don't may need startPeriod-only or a structure-version check; and how to handle the >800 MB XML flows that are skipped at parse time so they aren't permanently missing.

shiller.strategy_reason: Single overwrite-in-place .xls workbook (full 1871-present, ~118 KB) with no API and no partial download; correct pattern is re-download+overwrite the one parquet, gated on the file's vintage signal.
shiller.vintage_signal: HTTP Last-Modified (or content hash) of http://www.econ.yale.edu/~shiller/data/ie_data.xls; rebuild+overwrite shiller.parquet only when it moves (drop the skip-if-exists guard).
shiller.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/shiller/shiller.parquet (~118 KB, ~9 series). One dir, one unit.
shiller.rate_note: No key; single GET over plain http:// (not https), 120s timeout; hard dependency on the xlrd package to read legacy binary .xls; COLUMNS index mapping is hardcoded to the current sheet layout.
shiller.open_question: Does econ.yale.edu return a trustworthy Last-Modified for ie_data.xls, or should we hash the body to detect change? Also confirm xlrd remains installed in the runner.

sipri.strategy_reason: Single multi-sheet annual XLSX (~435 KB, all years 1949-present) with no API/partial download; re-parse+overwrite the one parquet on a new annual vintage, gated on the dated filename probe.
sipri.vintage_signal: Probe the dated bulk URL on sipri.org/www.sipri.org: HEAD/GET SIPRI-Milex-data-1949-<year>.xlsx auto-discovering current/next year (ahead of the hardcoded 2024/2023 list); first 200 with >10 KB is the live vintage, compare filename/Last-Modified to stored.
sipri.out_paths_note: Single file: data/clean_full/sipri/sipri.parquet (~435 KB). CAUTION: the same data/clean_full/sipri/ dir also contains milex.parquet written by a DIFFERENT script (sipri_polity) — do NOT 'clear the sipri dir'; delete only sipri.parquet.
sipri.rate_note: No key; HTTPS GET, 120s timeout, accepts first URL with >10 KB body; hard dependency on openpyxl; header-row/country-column detection is heuristic (could yield 0 obs if layout changes).
sipri.open_question: Confirm SIPRI's annual filename convention (always SIPRI-Milex-data-1949-<year>.xlsx, possibly with a _vX.Y suffix as seen in sipri_polity) so the vintage probe matches; verify sheet names are stable across vintages.

sipri_polity.strategy_reason: Three tiny annual bulk XLSX/XLS (SIPRI milex + Polity5 + MEPV) with no delta API; the right pattern is overwrite-single-file per source on a new vintage — drop the skip-if-exists guard and re-parse+overwrite, gated on a vintage signal. Not S6: hosts are fetchable (no 403/WAF/credential wall).
sipri_polity.vintage_signal: SIPRI: probe/compare the versioned dated filename SIPRI-Milex-data-1949-<year>_v<X.Y>.xlsx on www.sipri.org (404 = vintage moved) or its Last-Modified. Polity/MEPV: gate on Last-Modified of www.systemicpeace.org p5v2018.xls and MEPVv2018.xls (frozen 2018 vintages — poll for a newer file).
sipri_polity.out_paths_note: Multi-dir, three files: data/clean_full/sipri/milex.parquet, data/clean_full/polity/polity5.parquet, data/clean_full/polity/mepv.parquet. Note milex.parquet shares the sipri/ dir with the separate sipri source's sipri.parquet — overwrite per-file, never clear the dir.
sipri_polity.rate_note: No key; custom User-Agent set; RATE=0.5s between sources; www.systemicpeace.org historically flaky; SIPRI versioned filename and the SIPRI_SHEETS 'Constant (2024) US$' sheet name are hardcoded and may 404/mismatch on a new release.
sipri_polity.open_question: Polity5 and MEPV have been frozen at 2018 upstream — confirm whether systemicpeace.org will ever publish newer vintages (else these are effectively static and only need an occasional poll); and how to parameterize the hardcoded SIPRI versioned filename/sheet name for auto-vintage pickup.

social_progress.strategy_reason: Annual whole-dataset SPI with no delta API and ALL ~14 hardcoded source URLs dead (404/403, cdn.socialprogress.org DNS fails) so it produces 0 obs today; cannot be kept fresh automatically until a human supplies a live download URL.
social_progress.vintage_signal: none-poll-only: no working upstream URL or last-modified exists today; once a live SPI CSV/XLSX URL is supplied, gate on that file's HEAD Last-Modified/ETag (would become S5/S1).
social_progress.out_paths_note: writes single file data/clean_full/spi/spi.parquet — COLLIDES on the exact same path as the spi source (ingest_spi.py); last writer wins. Must reconcile to one owning script.
social_progress.rate_note: No API key; custom User-Agent; fetch() rejects HTML and returns None on 403/404.
social_progress.open_question: Two scripts (ingest_social_progress.py and ingest_spi.py) own the identical output path spi/spi.parquet — which one should be retired, and can a human supply a current working SPI download URL since every hardcoded URL is dead?

spi.strategy_reason: Sibling/duplicate of ingest_social_progress.py: annual whole-dataset SPI, no delta API, all 4 hardcoded URLs return HTTP 404 so 0 obs today; un-auto-fetchable until a human wires in a live source URL.
spi.vintage_signal: none-poll-only: no live URL or last-modified today; once a working SPI CSV/ZIP URL exists, gate on HEAD Last-Modified/ETag of that file (then S5/S1).
spi.out_paths_note: writes single file data/clean_full/spi/spi.parquet — SAME path as social_progress (ingest_social_progress.py); output-path collision, last writer wins.
spi.rate_note: No API key; custom User-Agent; defined-but-unused data.world TABLEAU_URL constant.
spi.open_question: Keep this script or ingest_social_progress.py (they clobber the same spi/spi.parquet)? And supply a current working SPI download URL, since all hardcoded URLs are 404.

ssb.strategy_reason: Statistics Norway PxWeb (data.ssb.no) exposes selectable time-dimension values, so a since=last_obs+1 period filter per table is mechanically feasible; pull only newer periods and merge per group rather than re-querying all time values.
ssb.vintage_signal: PxWeb per-table metadata 'updated'/last-modified field on data.ssb.no (GET table metadata) to decide whether to re-query; drive startPeriod off max stored obs_date per series.
ssb.since_param: PxWeb time-dimension value selection (filter:item on the time variable), set to values > max stored obs_date — PxWeb has no literal startPeriod token, so restrict the explicit time-value list to newer codes.
ssb.out_paths_note: per-group parquet files data/clean_full/ssb/grp_<subject>.parquet (~186 files, keyed by first 2 chars of table id) plus cached ssb/_catalog.json — writes to MANY group files; delta must read-existing, compute max obs_date, merge+overwrite each group.
ssb.rate_note: No API key; custom UA; RATE=0.25s between calls; HTTP 429 -> 30s sleep; MAX_CELLS=80000 cap downsamples oversized tables (time kept full).
ssb.open_question: Catalog is cached to _catalog.json and never re-crawled — should delta runs re-crawl the catalog (delete _catalog.json) to discover newly published tables, or only refresh known groups?

stat_estonia.strategy_reason: Statistics Estonia PxWeb v1 (andmed.stat.ee) supports time-dimension value sub-selection, so per-table since=last_obs delta is feasible; restrict the time selection to newer values and merge+overwrite each subject file instead of full re-pull.
stat_estonia.vintage_signal: PxWeb table last-modified/'updated' metadata on andmed.stat.ee (or a stored per-table watermark) to gate re-query; startPeriod derived from max stored obs_date.
stat_estonia.since_param: PxWeb time-variable value selection (filter:item on time) limited to codes > max stored obs_date; note query_table must use the path WITHOUT a trailing slash (trailing slash returns empty values).
stat_estonia.out_paths_note: per-subject parquet files data/clean_full/stat_estonia/<subject>.parquet (7 files: majandus, rahvastik, rahvaloendus, sotsiaalelu, keskkond, eri-valdkondade-statistika, Lepetatud_tabelid) plus cached _catalog.json — multiple subject files; merge per subject.
stat_estonia.rate_note: No API key; custom UA; RATE=0.3s; HTTP 429 -> 30s sleep; MAX_CELLS=100000 cap downsamples oversized tables (time full).
stat_estonia.open_question: Should delta runs re-crawl the BFS catalog (delete _catalog.json) to catch new tables, or trust the cache and only refresh existing subjects?

stat_latvia.strategy_reason: Statistics Latvia PxWeb v1 (data.stat.gov.lv, two databases OSP_PUB/OSP_OD) supports per-request time-dimension selection, so since=last_obs delta is feasible; restrict time selection to newer values and merge+overwrite each group file.
stat_latvia.vintage_signal: PxWeb per-table last-modified/'updated' metadata on data.stat.gov.lv (or stored watermark) to gate re-query; startPeriod from max stored obs_date.
stat_latvia.since_param: PxWeb time-variable value selection (filter:item on time) limited to codes > max stored obs_date; query_table uses a trailing slash on the URL for this source.
stat_latvia.out_paths_note: per-group parquet files data/clean_full/stat_latvia/<db>_<subject>.parquet (16 files; group = database OSP_PUB/OSP_OD + first path segment, e.g. OSP_PUB_POP, OSP_OD_arhivs) plus cached _catalog.json — spans TWO databases / many group files; merge per group.
stat_latvia.rate_note: No API key; custom UA; RATE=0.3s; HTTP 429 -> 30s sleep; MAX_CELLS=100000 cap downsamples oversized tables (time full).
stat_latvia.open_question: Catalog (BFS over both OSP_PUB and OSP_OD) is cached — should delta runs re-crawl both databases to discover new tables, or only refresh known groups?

stat_slovenia.strategy_reason: SURS PxWeb v1 (pxweb.stat.si SiStatData) supports selectable time-dimension values, so per-table since=last_obs delta is feasible; restrict time selection to newer values and merge+overwrite each group file rather than re-pulling all time.
stat_slovenia.vintage_signal: PxWeb per-table last-modified/'updated' metadata on pxweb.stat.si (or stored watermark) to gate re-query; startPeriod from max stored obs_date.
stat_slovenia.since_param: PxWeb time-variable value selection (filter:item on time) limited to codes > max stored obs_date; table id .px suffix is stripped when building the series-key prefix.
stat_slovenia.out_paths_note: per-group parquet files data/clean_full/stat_slovenia/<grp>.parquet (~143 files; group = first 3 chars of the .px table id, e.g. 021, 05G, 071) plus cached _catalog.json — many group files; merge per group.
stat_slovenia.rate_note: No API key; custom UA; RATE=0.3s; HTTP 429 -> 30s sleep; MAX_CELLS=100000 cap downsamples oversized tables (time full).
stat_slovenia.open_question: Catalog is a single flat GET cached to _catalog.json — should delta runs re-fetch it to catch newly published tables, or trust the cache?

statcan.strategy_reason: One of the 4 giants; getFullTableDownloadCSV is full-table only (no since param) but the WDS change-feed getChangedCubeList(date) lets us refresh only whole CHANGED cubes — the canonical S4 pattern for this source.
statcan.vintage_signal: StatCan WDS getChangedCubeList(<last_success_date>) change-feed (alternatively each cube's releaseTime from getAllCubesListLite) to select only cubes changed since last run; getAllCubesListLite is already re-enumerated each run so new cubes are caught.
statcan.since_param: n/a (S4 uses the getChangedCubeList change-feed to pick whole cubes to re-pull; for true intra-cube obs delta the alternative would be getBulkVectorDataByRange startRefPeriod=max stored obs_date, but base strategy is whole-changed-cube).
statcan.out_paths_note: per-cube files data/clean_full/statcan/<productId>.parquet (~8,207 cubes) plus _manifest.jsonl, _errors.log, _sizecache.json, _tmp/ staging and .done/.fail markers — one file per cube; S4 clears the .done marker for each changed cube only.
statcan.rate_note: No API key; polite UA; WDS soft limit ~25 req/s/IP; self-limits via SizeAwareGate (4 concurrent small, 1 exclusive large) + heavy-parse semaphore. SANDBOX HAZARD: concurrent large (>8MB) streaming downloads get the process killed by IO watchdog (hence exclusive large lane). Flags: --workers 1-6 (default 6), --budget, --presize, --dry.
statcan.open_question: .fail markers permanently suppress retries (404/BadZip/no-table) so a cube that later becomes available stays skipped until .fail is deleted — should the change-feed driven refresh also clear stale .fail markers for changed cubes?

statfin.strategy_reason: Statistics Finland StatFin PxWeb supports time-dimension value selection, so per-subject since=last_obs delta is feasible; restrict the time selection to codes newer than max stored obs_date and APPEND/merge into the subject parquet instead of re-pulling all time values.
statfin.vintage_signal: PxWeb per-table last-modified/'updated' metadata on the StatFin PxWeb API (or a stored per-subject watermark) to gate re-query; startPeriod from max stored obs_date. Catalog must be re-crawled (delete _catalog.json) to catch new tables.
statfin.since_param: PxWeb time-variable value selection limited to codes > max stored obs_date; requires adding per-subject state since the in-memory 'seen' dedup spans only one run, plus a per-subject append/merge step.
statfin.out_paths_note: single parquet per subject area data/clean_full/statfin/<subject>.parquet (~130 files) plus _catalog.json cache — many subject files; delta needs read-existing-max-date + append/merge per subject.
statfin.rate_note: No API key; CC BY 4.0; polite UA; RATE=0.3s; HTTP 429 -> 30s sleep; MAX_CELLS=100000 cap downsamples very large tables (single aggregate member per non-time dim).
statfin.open_question: Cadence is undeclared in SCHEDULE (tables update irregularly monthly/quarterly/annual) — confirm a monthly cron is acceptable, and whether delta runs should always re-crawl the catalog to detect new tables/subjects.

stats_nz.strategy_reason: Whole-series-per-file bulk CSVs from stats.govt.nz with NO server-side date param (matrix: delta must be client-side after download); gate on URL/HEAD availability and re-pull changed files.
stats_nz.vintage_signal: HEAD-probe the per-dataset CSV download URLs (currently hardcoded period strings like 'March-2025-quarter') and gate on HTTP 200 + Last-Modified/Content-Length; needs a calendar roll-forward so new period strings are probed newest-first instead of the frozen DATASETS_DYNAMIC list.
stats_nz.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/stats_nz/stats_nz.parquet (~330KB, ~12 curated datasets); partial coverage written silently if some dataset URLs fail to resolve.
stats_nz.rate_note: no API key, CC BY 4.0; 10s HEAD-probe timeout per candidate URL; no documented rate limit.
stats_nz.open_question: Period strings are hardcoded with no roll-forward — confirm the current stats.govt.nz URL path scheme for the latest quarter so new vintages are actually discovered (otherwise the pipeline 'succeeds' on year-old data).

swiid.strategy_reason: Small annual full-table CSV re-estimated end-to-end each release (history changes), so per-obs append would be wrong; correct refresh is detect-new-release then full overwrite (matrix-recommended).
swiid.vintage_signal: GitHub API latest commit SHA / release tag for data/swiid_summary.csv on fsolt/swiid (or Last-Modified on raw.githubusercontent GET); skip download when unchanged, overwrite atomically when SHA moves.
swiid.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/swiid/swiid.parquet (~67KB); series_key uses 30-char-truncated country NAME (not ISO3).
swiid.rate_note: no API key, CC BY 4.0; GitHub raw GET (HEAD 404s, code uses GET); no rate-limit concern at this volume.

tcmb.strategy_reason: Daily FX already date-driven: enumerates weekdays from last stored obs to today and fetches only the gap via a per-date URL path; canonical fetch-newer-and-append.
tcmb.vintage_signal: date-tail always-fetch: enumerate weekdays since max stored obs_date and GET tcmb.gov.tr/kurlar/{YYYYMM}/{DDMMYYYY}.xml; non-trading days 404 and are skipped.
tcmb.since_param: max stored weekday (obs_date) computed automatically from the parquet; manual window via --start=YYYY-MM-DD --end=YYYY-MM-DD; date is encoded in the {YYYYMM}/{DDMMYYYY}.xml URL path (from-to path), not a query param.
tcmb.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/tcmb/tcmb.parquet (~2.5MB, ~30 currencies x 4 rate types).
tcmb.rate_note: no API key; self-throttle RATE=0.05s (~20 req/s); no documented hard limit but full 1996-present rebuild is high request count (~7,800 weekdays).
tcmb.open_question: Persist non-trading-day 404s to a skip-set and switch checkpoint writes to temp+rename (current in-place pq.write_table has a small crash-time data-loss window) — improvements, not blockers.

transparency_ti.strategy_reason: Tiny annual full table; OWID grapher CSV returns ALL years each call so per-obs delta is meaningless — detect a new edition (newer max year) and overwrite (matrix-recommended).
transparency_ti.vintage_signal: Fetch OWID CSV ourworldindata.org/grapher/ti-corruption-perception-index.csv (ETag/Last-Modified or max-year compare vs stored parquet); rewrite only if a newer year appears. Generate the TI CDN xlsx fallback URL (CPI20XX) from current year instead of the hardcoded TI_URLS list.
transparency_ti.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/transparency_ti/transparency_ti.parquet (~4KB, ~180 countries x ~13 years); ISO3 falls back to sanitized entity name for aggregates.
transparency_ti.rate_note: no API key, CC BY; OWID CSV reliably public; TI CDN xlsx frequently 403 (fallback only, needs openpyxl).

treasury.strategy_reason: FiscalData API supports server-side date filtering (filter=record_date:gt:); matrix flags adding the since filter + append as a straightforward high-value fix to replace the full per-endpoint re-pull.
treasury.vintage_signal: per-endpoint server-side date filter: read existing parquet max obs_date and request only newer rows; underlying endpoints update at mixed freq (daily DTS, monthly MTS).
treasury.since_param: filter={date_field}:gt:{max_stored_date} (date_field is the endpoint's date column, e.g. record_date), with sort already set; paginated page[size]=10000.
treasury.out_paths_note: MULTI-FILE: per-endpoint (cube) parquet under data/clean_full/treasury/ (~181 files) plus _manifest.jsonl, _errors.log, _parts/ checkpoints; external catalog data/_treasury_catalog_final.json (new endpoints auto-detected, new rows in done endpoints not until .done cleared).
treasury.rate_note: no API key (US public domain); API unstable under load — Connection: close, MAX_ATTEMPTS=15 jittered backoff, page[size] cap 10000, 0.12s between pages, endpoint concurrency default 4 (--workers); RemoteDisconnected is main failure mode.
treasury.open_question: Each endpoint's date_field name must be resolved per endpoint to build the correct record_date:gt: filter; confirm the date column for endpoints whose date field is not literally 'record_date'.

ucdp.strategy_reason: Single annual CSV ZIP with no date/since param and a hardcoded versioned filename; a re-run cannot pick up new data — must detect a new vintage via the downloads listing and re-download+rebuild the whole (tiny) file.
ucdp.vintage_signal: scrape ucdp.uu.se/downloads/ for the latest ucdp-prio-acd-*-csv.zip filename/version and compare its version string / Last-Modified against a stored marker; full re-pull on change (currently ACD_URL hardcoded to v24.1 ucdp-prio-acd-241-csv.zip).
ucdp.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/ucdp/acd.parquet (~29KB, ~2,686 obs); main() skips if file exists so it must be deleted to refresh (no --force flag).
ucdp.rate_note: no API key; direct HTTPS with custom UA, 3 retries, 120s timeout; rate limit not a concern (one file).
ucdp.open_question: Confirm the ucdp.uu.se downloads page is scrapable for the latest versioned ACD zip filename (so a new vNN.N is auto-detected rather than hand-bumping ACD_URL).

un_wpp.strategy_reason: Whole-revision bulk CSV.GZ files (1950-2100 regenerated each revision) with no observation-level since param; gate on HEAD and re-pull both files on a new revision (matrix-recommended).
un_wpp.vintage_signal: HEAD the two CSV.GZ URLs for Last-Modified / Content-Length (or scrape the population.un.org CSV_FILES directory listing) and compare to a stored marker; currently both URLs hardcoded to the WPP2024 revision.
un_wpp.out_paths_note: MULTI-FILE: data/clean_full/un_wpp/indicators_medium.parquet (~25.9MB) and indicators_other.parquet (~114MB); each independently skip-if-exists guarded (both must be deleted to force re-pull); stray _wpp_log.txt/_wpp_err.txt sidecars.
un_wpp.rate_note: no API key; direct HTTPS streamed with custom UA, 300s timeout, 3 retries; handles .gz or .zip.
un_wpp.open_question: A new revision (e.g. WPP2026) requires editing BASE/FILES to the new filename pattern in addition to the HEAD check — confirm the next-revision URL scheme to fully automate detection.

undp_hdr.strategy_reason: Small annual table; the composite CSV already carries the full 1990-present series so per-obs delta is meaningless — detect a new edition and full-overwrite (cheap), gate on the edition-parameterized composite URL.
undp_hdr.vintage_signal: probe the composite time-series CSV URL with the edition/year parameterized (next edition, e.g. 2024-25) instead of hardcoded 2023-24; re-pull fully on a successful newer edition (optionally Last-Modified on the current composite URL); URLs currently hardcoded to the 2023-24 HDR.
undp_hdr.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/undp_hdr/undp_hdr.parquet (~1.5MB); keys {indicator}:{ISO3} from composite CSV or {hdi|gdi|gii|ihdi|mpi}:{iso} from annex XLSX.
undp_hdr.rate_note: no API key; direct HTTPS with custom UA, 120s timeout; annex XLSX path needs openpyxl; brittle multi-URL fallback (0 obs aborts without overwriting, leaving prior file intact).
undp_hdr.open_question: Confirm hdr.undp.org's next-edition composite-CSV URL/year naming pattern so edition detection can be parameterized rather than hand-editing BASE_URL/COMPOSITE_URLS/FILES.

unhcr.strategy_reason: Per-endpoint fetch already parameterizes &year={year}, so a server-side year filter lets us fetch only [max_year..current_year] and merge instead of re-looping 1951-2026.
unhcr.vintage_signal: date-tail always-fetch: read max obs_date from unhcr.parquet, then re-fetch the last ~2 years per endpoint (UNHCR revises recent years). No ETag/last-modified on the API, so the tail re-pull IS the change detector.
unhcr.since_param: &year={year} on fetch_endpoint_year(endpoint, year); iterate year from (max_obs_year-1) to dt.date.today().year per endpoint (population/idmc/solutions)
unhcr.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/unhcr/unhcr.parquet; keys are {endpoint}:{field}:{coo_iso}:{coa_iso} across 3 endpoints but all land in one parquet
unhcr.rate_note: no key; RATE=0.3s between pages/years, 429->sleep 30, 4 retries, PAGE=100, coo_all/coa_all bilateral pairs = many small requests
unhcr.open_question: Replace hardcoded current_year=2026 (line 119) with dt.date.today().year so future years aren't silently capped; confirm a 2-year revision lookback is enough for UNHCR back-revisions.

unsdg.strategy_reason: UN SDG Series/Data API exposes NO global since/updatedAfter/startPeriod, so S3 is infeasible; correct refresh is re-fetch series and overwrite the whole single-parquet table when a series grew.
unsdg.vintage_signal: per-series totalElements (from Series/Data paging metadata): compare API totalElements vs stored row count per series; re-pull and merge/overwrite only series whose totalElements grew. Poll-driven (no global last-modified).
unsdg.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/unsdg/unsdg.parquet (~18 MB), rewritten in full at each 100-series checkpoint; keys {seriesCode}:{geoAreaCode}|dim=val|...
unsdg.rate_note: no key; RATE=0.5s/series, 429->sleep 60, 4 retries, PAGE=1000; ~713 series, unstats.un.org SDG API slow/flaky
unsdg.open_question: Current resume model skips already-done series entirely, so revised/extended observations in existing series are silently stale; confirm switching to fetch-all + dedup on (series_key,obs_date) is acceptable (~713 series re-queried each run, still fast).

usda.strategy_reason: Substantive data is the NASS Quick Stats whole-database dated dumps (qs.<sector>_YYYYMMDD.txt.gz) with no since field; a new monthly vintage replaces the snapshot wholesale, so gate on the dated bulk file and re-ingest changed cubes.
usda.vintage_signal: new dated bulk file appearing under data/raw/usda (qs.<sector>_YYYYMMDD.txt.gz; current vintage 20260603), or HEAD Last-Modified/Content-Length on https://www.nass.usda.gov/datasets/qs.<sector>.txt.gz; on change delete the affected cube dirs (+_complete + _manifest.json) and re-ingest.
usda.out_paths_note: MULTI-DIR: per-cube part files under data/clean_full/usda/{animals_products,crops,demographics,economics,environmental}/part_NNN.parquet + per-cube _complete sentinel + _manifest.json. NOTE two scripts: bulk jobs/ingest_usda.py (this, S5) vs the orchestrated connectors/usda/connector.py (6 API queries, ignores --since, writes data/clean) — bulk pipeline is the real data source.
usda.rate_note: bulk path no key (curl public-domain .txt.gz); large refresh (57.6M rows), run via run_until_done.sh (MAX=60 restarts) due to sandbox killing long jobs. Orchestrated connector path alone needs a key.
usda.key_env: none for bulk pipeline; USDA_API_KEY only for the separate connectors/usda connector path
usda.open_question: Vintage refresh MUST delete cube dirs + _complete before dropping a new dated file (skip-rows resume mis-aligns on reordered snapshots) — confirm download_all.sh vintage bump + cube wipe is automated, not manual; decide whether to keep --with-census off (default, avoids dup rows).

vdem.strategy_reason: V-Dem ships as a single wide country-year RData regenerated per annual version with no obs-level since; correct refresh is release-detect on the GitHub repo and full re-pull+overwrite both parquets on change.
vdem.vintage_signal: GitHub API latest commit SHA of vdeminstitute/vdemdata master (api.github.com/repos/vdeminstitute/vdemdata/commits/master) or HEAD/ETag of raw.githubusercontent.com/.../master/data/vdem.RData; compare to stored marker, full re-pull on change.
vdem.out_paths_note: TWO files in one dir: data/clean_full/vdem/vdem.parquet (~40.6 MB) and vparty.parquet (~4.1 MB), independently guarded; keys VDEM:{variable}:{country_text_id}
vdem.rate_note: no key (public GitHub raw, custom UA, 300s timeout, streamed, 3 retries); needs pyreadr; large RData download+melt in 200-col chunks is the cost
vdem.open_question: Repo tracks unpinned 'master' so version can shift unannounced with no recorded vintage — pin to a release tag and record it, and remove the skip-if-exists guard that currently makes re-runs no-op.

wgi.strategy_reason: WGI is a single all-years World Bank Excel with no per-year endpoint; only correct refresh is re-download the whole workbook and overwrite atomically when a vintage signal moves.
wgi.vintage_signal: HTTP HEAD Last-Modified/ETag on the WGI_URLS candidate World Bank workbook URLs (or compare new workbook max year vs parquet max obs_date); replace the early-return existence guard with this check.
wgi.rate_note: no key; UA header set, 120s timeout, 3 retries, 4 candidate URLs (breaks on 403/404)
wgi.open_question: Currently no-ops because wgi.parquet exists (existence guard returns early); confirm replacing it with a Last-Modified/ETag gate, and that at least one of the 4 World Bank URLs still serves a non-stale workbook.

who_gho.strategy_reason: ghoapi is OData v4 and accepts a server-side date filter on TimeDim, so we can fetch only observations newer than each indicator's stored max year and merge — true obs-level delta.
who_gho.vintage_signal: date-tail: per-indicator max obs year from who_gho.parquet drives &$filter=TimeDim ge <last_year>; plus GET /api/Indicator set-difference to add wholly-new indicator codes. The TimeDim filter is the change detector.
who_gho.since_param: &$filter=TimeDim ge <last_obs_year> appended to fetch_indicator OData URL (alongside existing &$select=SpatialDim,TimeDim,NumericValue,TimeDimensionValue)
who_gho.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/who_gho/who_gho.parquet (~58 MB) + _who_gho_log.txt; keys CODE:GEO; checkpoints every 200 indicators overwrite same file
who_gho.rate_note: no key (ghoapi.azureedge.net); RATE=0.5s/indicator +0.1s/page, 429->60s, PAGE=1000 OData paging; cold ~3059-indicator pull is multi-hour; resume reads whole parquet into RAM
who_gho.open_question: Today the code only adds wholly-new indicators and never extends existing ones; confirm switching done-indicators from 'skip' to 'fetch TimeDim ge max_year then dedup on (series_key,obs_date)' is acceptable given the per-indicator extra calls.

whr.strategy_reason: WHR is an annual report delivered as whole XLSX/CSV panels with no row-level since; correct refresh is a freshness check + full overwrite when a new edition appears.
whr.vintage_signal: S3 XLSX Last-Modified/ETag on happiness-report.s3 panel URLs (with a worldhappiness.report Referer) and/or OWID grapher CSV ETag; or compare new workbook max year vs parquet max obs_date. Replace the early-return guard with this.
whr.out_paths_note: single file data/clean_full/whr/whr.parquet (~13 KB, currently only ~2,270 OWID Cantril-ladder obs) + multiple _whr_log*/_whr_err* side-cars
whr.rate_note: no key; S3 XLSX panels return 403 without a Referer from worldhappiness.report; most OWID grapher CSV slugs now 404
whr.open_question: COVERAGE BLOCKER: current output is only the ladder slice because all 6-factor S3 XLSX panels 403 and 6/7 OWID CSVs 404 — need a human to supply working panel URLs/Referer before any refresh, and the overwrite must compare obs counts so a thin pull doesn't clobber a richer prior file.

wid.strategy_reason: WID serves a whole-country bulk CSV (WID_data_{ISO}.csv) with no since filter; refresh is per-country whole-file re-download, gated per file so only changed countries rebuild.
wid.vintage_signal: HTTP HEAD Last-Modified/ETag (or Content-Length) per https://wid.world/bulk_download/WID_data_{ISO}.csv vs stored marker; re-download+overwrite only changed {CODE}.parquet. (No global manifest; per-file HEAD is the signal.)
wid.out_paths_note: MULTI-FILE per-country: data/clean_full/wid/<CODE>.parquet (119 present, ~270 codes); keys WID:{variable}:{percentile}:{age}:{pop}:{country}. WARNING: a legacy single wid.parquet (~328 MB) is never rewritten, stale, and DUPLICATES per-country data — dedup/exclude on load.
wid.rate_note: no key (wid.world/bulk_download); RATE=0.3s between countries, 3 retries+backoff, 120s timeout, 404->skip; cold full pull sizeable but each file 1-2 MB; no rate-limit blocker observed
wid.open_question: Change per-country skip-if-exists to always-overwrite (or HEAD-gated) so existing countries get new years; and delete the stale legacy wid.parquet to stop double-counting when the dir is loaded together.

wiid.strategy_reason: Single dated bulk XLSX (WIID-29APR2025) with NO date param; a new release is a new dated filename, so gate on discovering the latest WIID download link and re-download+rebuild only when the vintage advances.
wiid.vintage_signal: Discover latest WIID file link on the UNU-WIDER WIID database page (current hardcoded dated URL WIID-29APR2025); compare the dated filename / release tag to the stored one and re-download only when it changes. No in-code vintage check exists today.
wiid.out_paths_note: Single parquet data/clean_full/wiid/wiid.parquet (series_key=WIID:{variable}:{c3}); currently produces NO parquet (only _wiid_log.txt / empty _wiid_err.txt) because the fetch 403s.
wiid.rate_note: No API key; UNU-WIDER currently returns HTTP 403 to the plain requests UA on all 3 URLs (host UA-block, fixable with browser-like headers/Referer or a mirror, not a hard WAF/credential wall). 300s timeout.
wiid.open_question: Fix the live 403 first (add browser UA/Referer or mirror) AND replace the hardcoded WIID-29APR2025 URL + existence guard with latest-link discovery + a release-version gate; source is currently empty so it is the live silent-zero-coverage risk. If the 403 turns out to be an unbreakable WAF, reclassify to S6 manual_vintage.

wikidata.strategy_reason: Small (~22K entities) multi-file SPARQL snapshot that a full re-run refreshes correctly and cheaply; no usable server-side since param (Wikidata edits are continuous), so gate on a counts/vintage signal and overwrite atomically.
wikidata.vintage_signal: Run the SPARQL COUNT probes and compare per-cube published_totals against stored _manifest.json; skip the rewrite when counts are unchanged. (Note: count-only gating misses in-place attribute edits, so a periodic forced full re-pull is still advisable.)
wikidata.out_paths_note: Multi-file: data/clean_full/wikidata/{companies,stock_exchanges,currencies}.parquet + _manifest.json (series_key=QID). Separate scheduler path connectors/wikidata/connector.py emits a capped 250-company DEMO slice to data/clean/ — reconcile: the full pull is jobs/ingest_wikidata.py to clean_full, the connector is a demo and should not be the freshness source.
wikidata.rate_note: No key. Public WDQS SPARQL with strict limits: PAGE=1000, SLEEP_BETWEEN_PAGES=1.0s, MAX_RETRIES=6 honoring Retry-After, polite UA required; risk of 429/timeout on the larger companies cube.
wikidata.open_question: Add a guard so a transient WDQS hiccup returning fewer entities does NOT overwrite a previously-complete cube with a smaller snapshot (require new count >= stored count, else keep old).

worldbank_esg.strategy_reason: World Bank v2 API (source=75) honors a server-side date filter (sibling connector already wires since->date=YYYY:thisyear) AND exposes per-indicator lastupdated vintage; fetch only recent years and merge per indicator.
worldbank_esg.vintage_signal: Per-indicator meta['lastupdated'] (WB data vintage) already captured into _manifest.json; compare new lastupdated vs stored and only rewrite indicators whose vintage advanced.
worldbank_esg.since_param: date=<last_stored_year>:<current_year> on api.worldbank.org/v2 (drive last_stored_year from the manifest's per-indicator year_max), as connectors/worldbank_esg/connector.py does (since -> date=YYYY:thisyear).
worldbank_esg.out_paths_note: Per-indicator multi-file: data/clean_full/worldbank_esg/<IND>.parquet (71 files; country/obs_date/value) + _manifest.json; raw mirror data/raw/worldbank_esg/<IND>.json (71). Two scripts for this source_id: jobs/ingest_worldbank_esg.py (full, no date filter wired) vs connectors/worldbank_esg/connector.py (date filter wired) — reconcile by porting the connector's date wiring into the job.
worldbank_esg.rate_note: No key. urllib + UA, 6 retries exp backoff (cap 30s), 120s timeout, per_page=20000; 71 indicators pull in minutes, no rate-limit blocker observed.
worldbank_esg.open_question: If the live catalog enumeration transiently returns <71 indicators, only returned ones are rewritten and the rest are left orphaned (not pruned); also non-ISO3 country-name strings can leak in for unmapped aggregate codes — decide whether to prune or keep.

worldbank_extra.strategy_reason: Same World Bank v2 API; incremental_path confirms a date filter is feasible (append &date=YYYY:YYYY or mrv=1 to the country/all/indicator query), so fetch only the most-recent year(s) and overwrite-merge per source DB rather than re-pulling full history.
worldbank_extra.vintage_signal: No per-indicator last-updated field in the calls used; detect new data by re-pulling the most-recent year window (date-tail always-fetch) and merging — i.e. always fetch the open year and concat after dropping it. A full indicator-list scan is still needed to know WHICH indicators changed.
worldbank_extra.since_param: date=<last_stored_year>:<current_year> (or mrv=N) appended to fetch_indicator()'s country/all/indicator query on api.worldbank.org/v2.
worldbank_extra.out_paths_note: One zstd parquet per WB source DB under data/clean_full/worldbank_extra/ (hnp, ids, gfdd, gender, gem, edstats, poverty, jobs, doing_biz) — 9 units. Transient _<name>_ckpt.parquet/_<name>_done.json checkpoints during the run.
worldbank_extra.rate_note: No key, polite UA, self-throttles (0.1-0.3s sleeps, 4 retries w/ 8s*attempt backoff). Heavy pagination (gfdd ~8450 indicators, edstats ~3588) makes full runs slow; WB API is the rate constraint — the date-tail delta is the main cost win.
worldbank_extra.open_question: Not in daily_update.py SCHEDULE (effectively a manual one-shot backfill) — confirm desired cadence; and a partial/corrupt prior parquet is trusted by the skip-if-exists guard and never extended (must be deleted to redo).

worldbank_pink.strategy_reason: WB Pink Sheet ships a whole monthly XLSX workbook with NO date param (full history only); gate on the workbook vintage banner/doc id and re-download+rebuild only when it advances.
worldbank_pink.vintage_signal: Landing-page vintage doc id (FALLBACK_DOC, e.g. ...-0050012026) plus the 'Updated on ...' banner in xlsx row 4 (already captured into _manifest.json['vintage']); compare banner/doc id before re-downloading. Script currently re-downloads+overwrites unconditionally.
worldbank_pink.out_paths_note: 6 grouped parquet (m_price, m_index, a_price, a_index_nominal, a_price_real, a_index_real) under data/clean_full/worldbank_pink/ + _manifest.json; raw xlsx cached in data/raw/worldbank_pink/.
worldbank_pink.rate_note: No key, polite UA, 6 retries w/ backoff; requires openpyxl. Scrapes landing page for the live xlsx URL with a hardcoded FALLBACK_DOC (set 2026-06-04) fallback.
worldbank_pink.open_question: Silent-staleness risk: if the landing-page scrape breaks AND WB has rotated the doc id, the stale FALLBACK_DOC re-writes the SAME old vintage — add an alert when the scrape falls back to the hardcoded doc id.

worldbank_wdi.strategy_reason: Source access is the whole WDI_CSV.zip bulk with NO date param (full wide history); gate on the zip's HTTP vintage and re-download+rebuild the single parquet only when it changes.
worldbank_wdi.vintage_signal: HTTP HEAD Last-Modified / Content-Length on api.worldbank.org WDI_CSV.zip (fallback databank.worldbank.org/data/download/WDI_CSV.zip); no vintage check exists in code today, so add a HEAD gate before the ~tens-of-MB download.
worldbank_wdi.out_paths_note: Single zstd parquet data/clean_full/worldbank_wdi/worldbank_wdi.parquet (~60 MB, ~8.9M obs, series_key 'WDI:{ind}:{ctry}'). Written in 1M-row batches to ONE file (no actual file-splitting despite a commented >100M intent).
worldbank_wdi.rate_note: No key, polite UA, 300s timeout, 3 retries, two candidate URLs; rejects responses <100KB (api.worldbank.org bulk endpoint is occasionally flaky, hence the databank fallback).
worldbank_wdi.open_question: A prior truncated/partial parquet is trusted forever by the skip-if-exists guard (only a row-count sanity, no integrity check) — add a vintage/row-count assertion so a bad parquet is rebuilt.

yale_epi.strategy_reason: Tiny biennial index re-estimated each release; not hard-blocked, so gate on discovering a new epiYYYYresults.csv on the Yale downloads page and overwrite/append the new vintage (a hardcoded URL is explicitly NOT a manual_vintage case).
yale_epi.vintage_signal: Scrape https://epi.yale.edu/downloads for the latest epiYYYYresults.csv link and compare its year/filename to the stored vintage (currently hardcoded RESULT_URLS=[(epi2024results.csv,2024)]); a new year (e.g. 2026) triggers a pull. No catalog/last-modified probe exists today.
yale_epi.out_paths_note: Single zstd parquet data/clean_full/yale_epi/yale_epi.parquet (small; ~180 countries x ~40 indicators x year; series_key 'EPI:{var}:{iso3}'). Currently only 2024 is ever ingested.
yale_epi.rate_note: No key, polite UA, 60s timeout, SINGLE attempt per URL (no retry — a transient blip = 0 obs), rejects responses <500 bytes.
yale_epi.open_question: Confirm the 2026 release URL pattern when published and switch from skip-if-exists to read-existing+concat so multiple vintage years coexist; also add a retry since the no-retry single fetch can silently yield 0 obs and a moved/renamed 2024 URL would 404 to an empty file.

sec_edgar.strategy_reason: Access is two whole-file bulk zips from edgar/daily-index with NO date param on the zip endpoint; SEC refreshes them nightly, so gate on a HEAD vintage signal and re-download+rebuild only when changed (not a giant, so S4 is out; no server-side date filter on the bulk path, so S2 is out).
sec_edgar.vintage_signal: HEAD with descriptive UA on each bulk zip -- https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/daily-index/xbrl/companyfacts.zip and .../bulkdata/submissions.zip. Confirmed live: both return Last-Modified, ETag, and Content-Length. sec_edgar.out_paths_note: TWO stages / TWO dirs, and note: clean lands in clean_grouped NOT clean_full. Raw: data/raw/sec_edgar/companyfacts.zip + submissions.zip (~2.9GB) from fetch_sec_edgar_bulk.py. Clean: data/clean_grouped/sec_edgar/<TICKER>.parquet (~17,274 files, ~123M obs) from ingest_sec_edgar.py (clean_full/sec_edgar is empty). Re-parse overwrites all per-ticker parquets but never prunes -> tickers that vanish upstream leave orphan stale parquets.
sec_edgar.rate_note: No key, but SEC REQUIRES a descriptive User-Agent or returns 403 (set to 'Econ-Fin Data Library admin@hfdatalibrary.com'). SEC ~10 req/s fair-access limit -- not a constraint for a few large requests. 5 retries/file w/ 10s sleep, 1s gap between files, 120s timeout. Resume hazard: leftover .part is resumed via HTTP Range against the live URL; if upstream rotated the file mid-download the appended bytes corrupt the zip (no post-download integrity test) -- delete .part before any gated re-download.
sec_edgar.key_env: none (descriptive User-Agent header required; no API key/env var)
